The design seemed destined for historical footnote status until Donovan Limited, a small exploration company under contract with the Explorer Corps, discovered an abandoned example on CJW-7228, a small system three jumps off the Free Worlds League border, in the mid-3040s. Unable to refurbish the aging vehicle, Donovan Limited's board partnered with Miter Interstellar Research to reverse-engineer the design and develop a modern successor. The resulting Magellan program was shelved when the Clan Invasion disrupted Inner Sphere priorities, though the engineering work ultimately bore fruit through Interstellar Expeditions' investment.

The Cortez's legacy proves more durable than its survival record suggests. The SISO cargo philosophy, though never fully replicated in the Magellan line, shaped exploration vehicle development for centuries and demonstrated that commercial colonial platforms could carry operational capabilities rivaling dedicated military support vehicles.

text.overview: Death Trikes are handmade off-road vehicles designed only to propel weapon systems toward enemies at ludicrous speeds. Often the only advanced weapons available to pirates, the targeting system is the sole truly advanced component on these custom-kit vehicles. Considering their volatile superchargers, weapons, and complete lack of armor, Death Trikes are generally more dangerous to the pilot than anyone else.

The Deusenberg VIP Luxury Hovercar represents the modernized production configuration of a protected executive transport first introduced by the Federated Suns in 3024. Entering production in 3059 as an upgraded variant of the original design, this version incorporates a military-grade electronics suite and active anti-personnel systems reflecting the heightened security environment of the post-Clan Invasion Inner Sphere. Retaining the armored chassis and first-class passenger accommodations of its predecessor, the design continues to serve as a prestige transport for senior Federated Suns personnel and allied nobility, combining luxury and survivability with a limited electronic warfare capability suited to high-threat environments.
text.capabilities:
The 3059 configuration retains the medium hover chassis, fusion powerplant, and BAR 10 armor layout of the original Deusenberg, preserving the same cruise and flank speeds while upgrading all major systems to Tech D standards. The Armored Chassis Modification is carried forward, and armor distribution across the front, flanks, and rear is unchanged from the original design.

Where the original configuration devoted internal volume primarily to passenger comfort and cargo, this variant replaces most of that cargo space with a military-grade electronic suite. A Beagle Active Probe mounted at the front of the vehicle provides enhanced sensor coverage, capable of detecting concealed infantry and hidden vehicles well beyond normal sensor range. A Guardian ECM Suite occupies the right side, providing electronic countermeasures against missile guidance and fire-control systems that might target the vehicle or its escort. Three A-Pods mounted on the front, right, and left arcs deliver anti-personnel defense against infantry threats at close range.

First-class quarters accommodate the primary VIP passenger, and six passenger seats retain space for accompanying staff or security. Available cargo space is reduced to 1.55 tons by the electronic and defensive equipment, limiting logistical flexibility. An Equipment Rating of E/X-X-F reflects the classified nature of the vehicle's intelligence and ECM systems, restricting independent access to the design's core electronics.
text.deployment: The 3059 variant entered service with the Federated Suns command establishment as the prestige executive transport for flag-rank officers and senior nobility requiring active electronic protection in addition to armored mobility. Its Beagle Active Probe proved particularly valuable in the vanguard of high-security convoys, providing advance warning of ambushes and concealed threats that armor alone could not counter. The Guardian ECM suite added a further layer of protection against guided weapons. Deployed primarily at New Avalon and at major Federated Suns command installations, the vehicle continued in service well into the ilClan era, reflecting the durability of its upgraded specifications relative to the original configuration it replaced.
text.battleHistory:
The 3059 variant of the Deusenberg VIP Luxury Hovercar emerged from modifications applied to the Deusenberg One, the First Prince's personal limousine, during the post-Clan Invasion security review conducted across the Federated Commonwealth's executive fleet. Following the Battle of Tukayyid and the subsequent truce, security concerns for senior Federated Commonwealth leadership intensified considerably. Awareness that Clan forces remained concentrated across the border, combined with rising internal political tensions in the years before the Civil War, drove demand for vehicles that could combine executive comfort with active electronic countermeasures rather than passive armor alone.

The electronic upgrades applied to the Deusenberg One, incorporating a Beagle Active Probe and Guardian ECM suite alongside anti-personnel defenses, were judged sufficiently valuable to warrant inclusion in the standard New Avalon production line. The upgraded variant entered production in 3059, extending its security capabilities to a broader range of senior Federated Suns and Federated Commonwealth personnel beyond the First Prince's immediate household.

The 3059 design outlasted the original configuration by a considerable margin, remaining in production and service through the Civil War and Jihad eras as the authoritative Federated Suns VIP transport standard. New Avalon's production facilities avoided the catastrophic losses suffered by many other Federated Suns manufacturers during the Jihad, allowing uninterrupted output of the upgraded design. By the ilClan era, New Avalon's industrial arena had shifted considerably as political and commercial changes reshaped the former Federated Suns industrial base.

text.overview: The Deusenberg VIP Luxury Hovercar is a fifty-ton civilian hover transport commissioned by First Prince Hanse Davion of the Federated Suns in 3024. Conceived to provide Davion royalty and senior court personnel with a protected executive transport capable of operating in close proximity to military operations, the design blends first-class passenger accommodations with an armored chassis far exceeding ordinary civilian vehicle standards. Produced on New Avalon, the Deusenberg became the prestige conveyance of the Davion court and is perhaps best remembered for its central role in events surrounding the Fourth Succession War. Its unarmed configuration relies on speed and protection rather than firepower, prioritizing the survival of its occupants over independent combat capability.
text.capabilities:
The Deusenberg VIP Luxury Hovercar rides on a medium hover platform massing fifty tons, powered by a fusion powerplant that delivers a cruise speed of roughly seventy-five kilometers per hour and a flank speed approaching one hundred twenty kilometers per hour. This combination places it among the faster vehicles in its weight class, allowing the vehicle to clear most threat environments quickly without direct confrontation. The chassis carries an Armored Chassis Modification alongside just over three and a half tons of BAR 10 armor, providing meaningful protection against small arms and fragmentation while offering limited resistance to direct weapons fire. Frontal protection is prioritized, reflecting the assumption that the vehicle will typically be advancing toward or withdrawing from a threat rather than absorbing fire from multiple angles simultaneously.

Ten tons of first-class passenger quarters provide accommodations appropriate to royalty or senior military leadership, supported by six passenger seats for a security detail or accompanying staff. The remaining 6.05 tons of cargo capacity handles luggage, personal communications equipment, and mission-essential supplies. The original configuration carries no weapons, relying entirely on speed and armored protection for survivability. An Equipment Rating of D/X-F-D reflects the use of high-quality Federated Suns military-grade components, accessible to well-funded operators but not requiring cutting-edge technological infrastructure to maintain.
text.deployment: The original Deusenberg VIP Luxury Hovercar served throughout its operational life as the designated executive transport for Federated Suns and, after 3028, Federated Commonwealth senior leadership. Without weapons and with accommodations scaled for VIP passengers rather than military personnel, the design saw no front-line combat service, appearing instead in command-zone convoys, planetary capital circuits, and high-security installations where its combination of speed and armored protection made it a credible executive vehicle without demanding dedicated military escort. The design's Obsolete quirk, triggered in 3068, reflects its formal retirement from production as newer variants and alternative designs entered the Federated Suns executive fleet.
text.battleHistory:
The Deusenberg VIP Luxury Hovercar traces its origins to 3024, when First Prince Hanse Davion of the Federated Suns quietly commissioned a new class of armored limousine intended to impress the nobility of his entourage while providing genuine protection for senior personnel he planned to bring within range of active military operations. Davion was at the time preparing what would become the Fourth Succession War, and he understood that managing the Federated Suns and Lyran Commonwealth aristocracy accompanying him, none of them trained MechWarriors, would require a vehicle capable of surviving battlefield proximity without demanding military expertise from its occupants. Produced on New Avalon, the Deusenberg entered court service before hostilities commenced.

The vehicle became inseparably associated with the events of 3028, when Hanse Davion wed Melissa Steiner at a ceremony that also marked the opening of the Fourth Succession War. At this ceremony, Davion made his legendary declaration to his bride, announcing that his wedding gift to her was the Capellan Confederation itself. His words, "In honor of our marriage... I give you a vast prize. I give you the Capellan Confederation!", were destined to ring throughout history as a symbol of the age. Davion was well aware of the tempest he was inciting, and the Deusenberg's protective capabilities were not merely decorative during those dangerous years.

The most celebrated individual example of the type, designated the Deusenberg One, served as the First Prince's personal limousine from its commissioning until the vehicle's loss in the Jihad era. Hauptmann Gershvin Jackson served as its driver and caretaker until his death in 3051, considering his position and duties a matter of personal honor despite never having met the Prince directly. Following Hauptmann Jackson's death, the vehicle was modified during the 3050s to add enhanced electronics and active anti-personnel defenses suited to the elevated threat environment of the post-Clan Invasion era. After Katherine Steiner-Davion's assumption of power on New Avalon, the Deusenberg One fell into disrepair and was subsequently lost. It was last reported as of late 3062, its whereabouts unknown. The original configuration of the design was declared obsolete in 3068 as the Federated Suns' vehicle fleet modernized during the Jihad.

text.overview: The Dillinger Police Vehicle is a forty-ton hover support vehicle designed and built by Kressly Warworks on Epsilon Eridani in 3059. Created at the direct request of planetary president Pierre Benton, the vehicle was intended to give local police forces a credible and visible presence in cities overwhelmed by rising crime during the instability of the Chaos March period. Kressly's engineers deliberately expanded the vehicle's physical footprint beyond its strictly functional requirements, producing a hovercraft large enough to tower over civilian traffic and signal authority before a single officer stepped out. Although intended purely for law enforcement, its military-grade components gave it durability well suited to the volatile conditions of an independent world, and its blend of command, medical, and transport capabilities quickly attracted interest from buyers across the Inner Sphere.
text.capabilities:
The Dillinger is a hover support vehicle built around a fusion engine, giving it effectively unlimited operational range without refueling constraints. A cruise speed of seventy kilometers per hour allows it to respond rapidly across an urban area while still maintaining the imposing bulk that defines its visual deterrent role. Two tons of armor rated to BAR 10 provide meaningful protection against the small arms and light weapons most commonly encountered in riot and criminal interdiction environments, and an Armored Chassis Modification further reinforces the vehicle's structural integrity against improvised attacks.

For self-defense, the vehicle carries four military-grade machine guns distributed across its hull: one mounted in a roof turret for overhead engagement, one fixed forward, and one on each side. A single ton of ammunition supports extended patrols before resupply is required. The guns are loaded with rubber projectiles as standard but carry live ammunition as well, giving commanders flexibility in how they respond to escalating situations.

Three integrated support systems define the Dillinger's operational role. A ton of military-grade communications equipment provides encrypted tactical coordination, allowing the vehicle to serve as a mobile command post directing multiple units across a district. Paramedic equipment is fitted in the rear compartment for immediate casualty treatment. A rear-access cargo bay provides space for police equipment and supplies, while a forward infantry compartment can carry over a dozen officers directly to an incident. The vehicle's Distracting design quirk reflects its intentionally overwhelming presence.
text.deployment: The Dillinger serves law enforcement and paramilitary police roles in urban environments, functioning primarily as a mobile command post capable of directing operations across an entire district from a single vehicle. Its infantry transport capacity allows a full squad to be delivered directly to an incident without exposing officers to ambush during approach. Beyond law enforcement, individual units have found use as armored executive transport, emergency response coordination platforms, and tactical headquarters for small garrisons without dedicated command vehicles. The design is most commonly encountered operating alone or in pairs at the precinct level, though the Word of Blake Protectorate deployed them in coordinated groups as part of broader civil control operations across occupied worlds.
text.battleHistory:
The political dissolution of the Sarna March left Epsilon Eridani adrift as an independent world within the Chaos March, and the withdrawal of interstellar oversight brought a rapid deterioration in public order. The counties and palatinates of the planet found their local police forces wholly inadequate to contain the surge of criminal activity that accompanied the collapse of central authority. President Pierre Benton recognized that his Eridani Guards could not simultaneously address conventional military threats and rampant street crime, and in 3059 he contracted Kressly Warworks to develop a dedicated law enforcement platform.

Kressly's design entered production at their Epsilon Eridani factory and was issued to police departments across the planet's cities, where the vehicle's mass and military-grade systems gave law enforcement a degree of credibility their conventional equipment could not provide. Exports followed quickly. Free Worlds League police departments purchased the Dillinger in significant numbers before the Jihad, with the largest concentrations appearing on Irian, where corporate executives found the vehicle's armored bulk equally suited to use as a super-heavy limousine. The design's reputation for reliability in unstable environments made it a natural fit for any world experiencing civil unrest.

The Word of Blake's absorption of Epsilon Eridani during the Jihad brought the Kressly factory under Protectorate control. A team of Federated Suns researchers visiting the factory at the time of annexation disappeared without explanation, their fate unconfirmed. The Protectorate subsequently distributed the Dillinger to police forces across its territory, using the vehicle's conspicuous profile and law enforcement association to reinforce an image of civil order throughout worlds under Blake governance. By the end of the Jihad the Dillinger was present on every significant police force within the former Protectorate.

text.deployment: Configuration One mounts a Hyper-Velocity Autocannon/2 paired with an MML-5 launcher equipped with Artemis IV fire control, both in a turret. The multi-missile launcher accepts both LRM and SRM ammunition, giving the crew flexibility to engage at varying ranges, while the Artemis guidance improves accuracy across both missile types. Advanced Fire Control governs both weapons. The trailer is crewed by four gunners quartered aboard the tractor. Its twenty-ton cargo bay, accessed through four doors, is reserved for standard merchandise. Train 838 routinely deploys two Configuration One trailers as part of its standard consist on general cargo runs.

Configuration Two arms its turret with an Extended LRM-10 and an SRM-6 launcher, governed by Advanced Fire Control. The combination provides effective firepower across both long and short engagement ranges, with the extended-range missiles engaging threats at distance while the SRM rack handles adversaries that close to direct engagement range. Four gunners crew this configuration, quartered aboard the tractor. Its twenty-ton cargo bay carries eighteen tons of liquid freight, making this trailer the primary bulk liquid transport in the consist. Train 838 fields two Configuration Two trailers alongside its Configuration One modules, relying on this variant's dual-range capability as its primary combat response.

Configuration Three mounts an Extended LRM-5 paired with a Streak SRM-6 in its turret, both governed by Advanced Fire Control. The Streak guidance system improves hit probability against maneuvering targets, making this configuration well-suited to engagements against faster raider vehicles. Six gunners crew this configuration, reflecting the heavier crew demand of its weapons suite. Its twenty-ton cargo bay carries just over seventeen tons of refrigerated materials, supporting the Hegemony's food distribution network on Alphard's longer routes. Train 520 routinely operates two Configuration Three trailers, pairing them with Configuration Four modules for a consist balancing precision missile fire with direct autocannon capability.

Configuration Four replaces the missile-centric approach of other trailer types with a Hyper-Velocity Autocannon/5 and a Rocket Launcher 15, both in a turret governed by Advanced Fire Control. The heavier autocannon delivers substantially greater kinetic striking power against vehicle-class threats than the HVAC/2 carried by the tractor and Configuration One. The rocket launcher provides a burst-fire supplement for close engagements. Six gunners crew this configuration. Its twenty-ton cargo bay carries just under seventeen tons of livestock, serving Alphard's agricultural supply lines. Train 520 pairs two Configuration Four trailers with its Configuration Three modules, using this variant's hard-hitting autocannon as its primary anti-vehicle capability.

text.capabilities:
The Dreadnought Mk II tractor is built on a 200-ton tracked chassis with both Tech D chassis and armor construction, reinforced with eight tons of commercial grade ATC armor rated at BAR 7. This protection substantially exceeds the unmodified Elite Series 3 baseline and allows the vehicle to withstand repeated strikes from medium-class weapons. A fusion power plant provides sustainable mobility for convoy operations, drawing on the same engine to power any attached trailer modules. The tractor's primary armament mounts two Hyper-Velocity Autocannon/2s and two Extended LRM-5 launchers in the central turret, providing both close-range autocannon fire and the ability to engage threats before they reach optimal direct-fire distance. Six machine guns in front sponson mounts, coordinated by Machine Gun Arrays, provide area suppression against boarding parties and raider infantry. Advanced Fire Control governs all weapons systems.

The crew of twenty-seven is distributed across officer quarters, enlisted berths, and dedicated gunner stations. Two infantry bays carry a fifty-soldier security element for deployment at fueling stops or to repel boarders. Three steerage-class quarters accommodate fifteen additional personnel, while an onboard field kitchen allows extended operations without forward supply bases. A four-ton cargo bay at the rear, accessed through a rear door, typically carries food and medical supplies for the convoy. A three-ton lift hoist at the rear assists with cargo handling and trailer servicing during stops.
text.deployment: The Dreadnought Mk II tractor serves as the armored command vehicle and primary weapons platform for each land train convoy. Each tractor operates with two to four trailer modules, with Train 838 typically running two Configuration One and two Configuration Two trailers on Alphard's ore routes, and Train 520 most commonly deploying two each of Configurations Three and Four. Trailer configurations are exchanged between specific cargo runs to suit anticipated threat profiles. The tractor crew manages all turret weapons while dedicated trailer gunners handle their respective module armament, with all gunner personnel quartered aboard the tractor itself. The infantry bays allow rapid deployment of a security element at fueling stops or to repel boarding actions along remote stretches of route.

text.overview: The Dromedary Water Transport is a large wheeled support vehicle designed by New Vandenberg Autoworks for the Taurian Concordat during the Age of War. Introduced in 2562, the 150-ton vehicle serves as a bulk water tanker for arid Periphery worlds where reliable freshwater infrastructure does not exist. Built around a modified dune buggy chassis scaled up to commercial proportions, the Dromedary prioritizes ruggedness and simplicity over speed or sophistication. Its deliberately uncomplicated engineering has earned it a reputation as one of the most dependable civilian transports operating on the fringe of settled space, a workhorse valued precisely because it demands so little from its operators.
text.capabilities:
The Dromedary's dune buggy derived chassis gives it the ability to traverse harsh desert terrain that would strand conventional wheeled transports. Its oversized suspension and broad wheelbase distribute the vehicle's considerable weight across loose sand and broken ground, though this capability comes at the cost of speed. A top velocity of only 32 kilometers per hour makes the Dromedary one of the slower vehicles in its class, a trade-off the designers accepted given that the treacherous terrain it regularly crosses rarely permits faster travel regardless of a vehicle's theoretical performance.

The internal combustion engine is deliberately simple, requiring minimal maintenance and allowing field repairs with basic tools. A single fuel load provides a range exceeding 2,500 kilometers, enabling the Dromedary to make extended journeys between remote settlements without refueling. The primary cargo consists of a 50-ton liquid tank capable of carrying approximately 45 kiloliters of water, supplemented by four tons of standard cargo space for spare parts and crew supplies. Defensive provisions are minimal, limited to a turret-mounted machine gun and four tons of commercial-grade armor rated at BAR 5. This protection can deflect small arms fire and deter opportunistic bandits, but offers little resistance against military-grade weapons, forcing operators to rely on armed escorts when traversing particularly dangerous routes.
text.deployment: The standard Dromedary serves as a dedicated water hauler, ferrying bulk freshwater to communities that lack wells, rivers, or functioning purification systems. Most operate along established trade routes connecting settlements to water sources, though the vehicle's off-road capability allows it to reach sites well beyond maintained roads. Operators frequently customize their vehicles, with some installing secondary tanks for transporting specialty liquids, industrial chemicals, or refined fuels. These modifications have expanded the Dromedary's commercial appeal beyond simple water delivery, though the standard water transport configuration remains by far the most common.
text.battleHistory:
New Vandenberg Autoworks created the Dromedary in 2562 to address a persistent logistics problem across the Taurian Concordat's more remote holdings. Many Periphery worlds are arid planets where surface water is scarce or nonexistent, and settlements depend entirely on water shipped in from off-world or hauled overland from distant sources. Previous attempts to establish reliable ground transport across these desert environments had failed repeatedly, with conventional tanker vehicles becoming mired in loose sand or breaking down in the punishing conditions. NVA's solution was to adapt proven dune buggy suspension technology to a large-scale commercial vehicle, creating a transport that could handle the worst terrain the Periphery had to offer.

The design proved so effective that NVA never found reason to significantly alter it. Over half a millennium of continuous production has seen only minor refinements to the basic platform, proof of how well the original engineering matched the operating environment. The Dromedary's rusted-out hulks dot trade routes across the Periphery, marking where older vehicles finally succumbed to corrosion and neglect after years of service. Despite this attrition, steady production from New Vandenberg has kept the vehicle in widespread use.

The Dromedary's most celebrated individual vehicle is the Traveling Oasis, a water hauler operating on Atreus Prime in the Taurian Concordat. Primarily tasked with delivering water to uranium miners in the Dry Gulch Wastes, the Traveling Oasis also serves double duty as a militia supply vehicle. When pirates threaten the region, the vehicle accompanies local militia forces into the desert, providing logistical support while the militia hunts down the raiders. The troops stationed with the Traveling Oasis have developed a tradition of using whatever water remains after a mission to create an improvised swimming hole, a small luxury that has made the vehicle a favorite assignment among Atreus Prime's defenders.

text.overview: Dune buggies have been a mainstay of militias for countless centuries. Apart from jeeps, few other vehicle classes are more reliable and sturdy in off-road battle. Outfitted with an open gunner's station, dune buggies are very effective against other light vehicles and infantry, especially in the shifting sands of a desert or beachfront terrain. Not only pirate bands refit civilian vehicles into fighting machines.

The Dunning Mobile Tactical Command Post was among the earliest purpose-built mobile command vehicles, commissioned during the formative years of the Terran Hegemony. Produced by Altheon Ballistic Dynamics on New Earth under the supervision of engineer Domingo Halleburton, the Dunning was designed to give field generals a complete picture of the battlespace while operating near the front lines. Its chassis was based on an extended armored personnel carrier with a proven wheeled suspension, chosen for ease of maintenance and superior mobility across most terrain types. The Dunning represented a foundational step in battlefield coordination technology, providing capabilities that would inform the design of mobile headquarters vehicles for centuries to come.
text.capabilities:
Built with what would later be classified as primitive technology, the Dunning nonetheless carried seven tons of communications equipment that provided solid coordination capability for its era. The vehicle's improved communications systems could link ground forces with orbital assets and adjacent formations across a wide area. An off-road chassis modification improved mobility on unprepared surfaces, though the vehicle's internal combustion engine consumed fuel rapidly due to its inherent inefficiency, making the half-ton fuel system a persistent limitation during extended operations.

The Dunning carried no armament whatsoever, relying entirely on its BAR 6 armor and escort forces for protection. A three-ton infantry compartment housed security personnel or additional communications staff. The vehicle required an eleven-member crew, including two officers and nine enlisted technicians, to operate its full communications suite. Despite its seemingly civilian construction, the Dunning's communications payload gave commanders coordination capability that was unmatched by any ground-based system of the era, justifying its priority production status in the early Hegemony military.
text.deployment: The Dunning served the Terran Hegemony Armed Forces from 2317 through the late Age of War, with upgraded and field-modified examples persisting in secondary roles well beyond their intended service life. Civilian variants found use with planetary governments, emergency services, and media organizations across Hegemony space. The vehicle was rendered obsolete by approximately 2650 as more capable command platforms entered service. No Dunnings are known to survive in the modern era, though the design's influence on subsequent mobile headquarters vehicles is well documented.
text.battleHistory:
After Admiral James McKenna forcibly dissolved the Terran Alliance and established the Terran Hegemony, military reforms began reshaping the armed forces into a professional fighting force. The Campaigns of Persuasion that brought more than forty worlds under Terran control demonstrated the need for superior battlefield coordination. Field Marshal Mears Coblitz, Commanding General of the Hegemony Armed Forces, commissioned the Dunning as one of his first new equipment programs.

Initially destined only for division-level commanders, McKenna's campaigns in 2316 and 2317 showed that lead assault regiments required the same command capabilities. Coblitz requested sufficient Dunnings for every regiment, brigade, and higher-level formation. The first expanded production run was distributed in time for McKenna's second major campaign in 2320, where the Dunning played a major role in coordinating multi-regiment operations. The vehicle served the Hegemony military for well over a century, surviving throughout the Age of War in upgraded and field-modified forms. Within a decade of its introduction, Dunnings and virtual clones appeared in service with planetary governments, police forces, fire departments, civilian relief agencies, and entertainment organizations across Hegemony space. The vehicle was rendered obsolete by 2650, replaced by more capable designs that built upon its pioneering communications architecture.

text.overview: The Durandel-British "Blue Nova" Convertible is a small wheeled civilian vehicle introduced in 3067 as an affordable entry point into the high-performance sports car market. Manufactured by Durandel-British, the design was conceived to bring the excitement of motorsport culture to average consumers who had been priced out of the premium vehicle segment. Available in both hardtop coupe and convertible configurations, the Blue Nova quickly became one of the manufacturer's best-selling models and earned the informal title of "the everyman's sportster" from automotive reviewers. Its combination of sporty styling and accessible pricing found a receptive audience among driving enthusiasts across the Inner Sphere.
text.capabilities:
The Blue Nova is powered by a re-engineered 2750-model Outworlds Motors internal combustion engine, a utility vehicle powerplant adapted for the consumer sports car market. The 765-kilogram engine drives the 1,500-kilogram vehicle to a cruise speed of roughly 80 kilometers per hour with a flank speed of 120 kilometers per hour, making it considerably slower than purpose-built racing vehicles. Durandel-British partially compensates for the engine's modest output through a carefully engineered custom exhaust system that creates a convincing aural impression of greater power, though the vehicle is widely acknowledged to be underpowered in practice.

The convertible variant features a convertible chassis modification with seating for one driver and one passenger. BAR 2 rated armor provides minimal protection suited to the vehicle's purely civilian role. Fuel range of 379 kilometers on petrochemical fuel is adequate for daily commuting and recreational driving. Optional equipment packages include leather interior upholstery, a trivid entertainment system, and nitrous injectors. Even fully loaded with every available option, the convertible still costs slightly less than a base-model Scion-Nissaki Hyperion, preserving the Blue Nova's core value proposition. The vehicle offers 198 kilograms of standard cargo capacity through a single rear door.
text.deployment: The Blue Nova serves as a civilian sports car and personal transport vehicle. Popular among middle-class enthusiasts and casual drivers across the Inner Sphere, the vehicle is commonly found in urban centers and suburban communities wherever a market for affordable performance vehicles exists. The convertible model proved particularly sought after, with demand initially outstripping available supply following the vehicle's debut.
text.battleHistory:
Durandel-British developed the Blue Nova in response to growing consumer interest in high-performance vehicles during the late 3060s. Prior to its introduction, the sports car market was dominated by expensive manufacturers such as Avanti, Hughes-McCandless, and Scion-Nissaki, whose products remained well beyond the reach of ordinary citizens. The Blue Nova's 3067 debut changed this dynamic by offering a vehicle that delivered the appearance and appeal of a premium sports car at a significantly lower price point, costing nearly twenty percent less than the popular Starfire.

The key to the design's affordability was the manufacturer's decision to adapt an older utility vehicle powerplant rather than commissioning a new purpose-built engine. This cost-saving approach, paired with targeted compromises in outright performance, allowed Durandel-British to reach a price bracket that opened the market to a much broader customer base. The trade-off in raw speed was readily accepted by buyers who valued style and accessibility over track capability.

Consumer reception was immediate and enthusiastic. The Thorin Consumer's Review praised the vehicle as an accessible way to participate in high-performance vehicle culture. The distinctive shimmer paint option, which blends two opposite colors using polymer technology to create shifting hues depending on viewing angle, became particularly popular and helped establish the Blue Nova's visual identity. Consumers interested in the full experience could opt for the convertible model with all available options, though the base hardtop coupe proved equally popular for its clean styling.

text.overview: The Eagre is truly an all-purpose vehicle. Nominally developed as a fire engine employed by specialized infantry in the Avalon Hussars, it is also a very sturdy, general-use all-terrain vehicle. Battery-powered, it eschews volatile fuels, and is generously armored to address its potential combat support duties, making it a true boon to the support elements of FedSuns RCTs.

text.deployment: The standard Estevez served as the primary main battle tank of the Federated Suns throughout the twenty-fourth century. Typically deployed along border regions and in garrison postings, the base model was optimized for direct engagement of enemy armored vehicles and fixed fortifications. Its deep ammunition reserves suited it to sustained operations far from established supply lines, and the vehicle's imposing profile alone was often sufficient to deter lightly armed opponents from pressing an engagement.
text.battleHistory:
The Estevez entered service in 2310 and quickly became the backbone of armored forces across the nascent Federated Suns. During the sporadic border conflicts of the pre-Age of War period, the tank exemplified what contemporaries called "tank shock." Its imposing bulk and massive main cannon caused many opposing forces to break formation and retreat rather than stand against it. Some military historians later argued that the Federated Suns was built upon the Estevez rather than upon the ideals of the "Six Liberties," evidence of the vehicle's outsized role in securing the young nation's borders. The Free Worlds League recognized the design's effectiveness and produced a licensed copy designated the Kestrel MBT, which was identical in combat capability.

By the early 2400s, advancing military technology had rendered the Estevez obsolete. Its main weapon proved increasingly ineffective against modern armor compositions, and the inability to fire specialized munitions left it at a growing tactical disadvantage. The vehicle's substantial logistical demands further strained the resources of the Federated Peacekeeping Forces, while opponents discovered that targeting the tracks could disable and bypass even an otherwise intact tank.

The Estevez's only encounter with BattleMechs occurred during a Draconis Combine deep raid on Robinson. The Kuritan commander, a firm believer in the Ares Conventions, proposed the engagement be conducted with simulated munitions. The Combine 'Mechs overwhelmed the Estevez MBTs with ease and achieved their objective without difficulty. Subsequent analysis determined that even with live ammunition, a full regiment of tanks could not have defeated the Kuritan heavy 'Mech battalion. The demonstration confirmed what many military planners already suspected: conventional armor of the Estevez's generation was hopelessly outclassed by BattleMech technology.

Following its withdrawal from frontline service, a number of Estevez hulls received new turrets mounting lighter autocannon for use as anti-aircraft platforms. This conversion provided a modest extension of service life in the garrison role, but the aging chassis could not be economically maintained alongside newer equipment. By the mid-twenty-fifth century, the Federated Suns had retired the Estevez entirely in favor of the Tiger medium tank, and all remaining vehicles were scrapped.

text.deployment: Introduced in 2360 as a second-line garrison conversion, the Anti-Aircraft variant replaced the standard turret armament with a pair of light-class autocannon and three tons of ammunition, retaining a single machine gun for close defense. The modification was intended to extend the Estevez's service life by repurposing aging hulls for air defense duties, a role where the chassis's obsolescent ground combat capabilities mattered less. The refit ironically provided a modest increase in sustained firepower compared to the original configuration, but this was insufficient to justify continued maintenance of the fuel-hungry platform. The Anti-Aircraft model saw limited garrison service before being retired alongside the remaining standard variants.
