text.overview: A flatbed railcar (or flatcar) is a type of open-deck freight car designed without sides, roofs, or ends, featuring a simple, flat platform for carrying large, heavy, or irregularly shaped cargo. They are essentially flat, versatile platforms used for transporting goods that do not require protection from the weather.

The Freedom 900 Hover Jeep is the current production model of the Freedom series of utility hover vehicles, manufactured by Earthwerks Incorporated and sold across the Inner Sphere. The Freedom series has been in continuous production since the late twenty-seventh century, establishing a reputation for simplicity and durability that has made it the most widely distributed civilian hover vehicle in known space. The Freedom 900 is a refinement of that long heritage, introduced in 3013 as a four-seat utility platform designed for maximum accessibility across every economic tier of Inner Sphere society. Earthwerks' dominance of the hover utility market has made the Freedom 900 as common a sight on developed worlds as on struggling fringe planets, serving roles ranging from personal transport to emergency services.
text.capabilities:
The Freedom 900 is a 3,000-kilogram hover vehicle built around an internal combustion engine, prioritizing reliability and ease of maintenance over raw performance. Its cruise speed and moderate top speed are unremarkable by military standards but entirely adequate for its intended civilian applications. The design carries meaningful structural armor rated to withstand routine hazards, far more than its stablemate the Bayamo, making it genuinely suitable for rough terrain and environments where incidental damage is likely.

A Convertible Chassis Modification allows the Freedom 900 to be configured as a fully enclosed four-seat passenger vehicle, with a crew position and three dedicated passenger seats. The design carries 304 kilograms of standard cargo. Its fuel tank holds sufficient ICE fuel for approximately 2,564 kilometers of range, one of its most practical attributes for long-distance travel on worlds with sparse infrastructure. No weapons are fitted in the standard configuration, though the vehicle's cargo capacity and sturdy chassis have made it a common base for field modifications and specialty variants across its long production history. The rugged, uncomplicated powertrain requires minimal specialist tools to maintain, a feature Earthwerks has consistently highlighted in its marketing and one that has proven decisive in keeping the Freedom series dominant across underdeveloped worlds.
text.deployment: The Freedom 900 is found on virtually every inhabited world in the Inner Sphere in some form, from personal family transports to municipal utility fleets. Earthwerks has developed an extensive catalog of factory variants to serve specific markets, including multi-purpose vehicles, light cargo conversions, law enforcement configurations, and ambulance models. The basic platform's combination of range, carrying capacity, and low maintenance requirements makes it particularly prevalent on frontier worlds and developing colonies where specialized vehicles are unavailable. Military and paramilitary organizations occasionally use Freedom 900 variants for logistics, courier duty, and base transport in rear-echelon roles where the vehicle's lack of armor and weapons is not a disqualifying factor.
text.battleHistory:
The Freedom series traces its origins to the late twenty-seventh century, when Earthwerks Incorporated identified the civilian hover utility market as an underserved segment of the Inner Sphere economy. Early Freedom models established the design philosophy that would carry through every subsequent iteration: simple engineering, low production costs, broad-market pricing, and a chassis robust enough to survive decades of hard use without specialized maintenance. The formula proved enormously successful, and the Freedom line became one of Earthwerks' most durable commercial properties over the following centuries.

The Freedom 900 was introduced to the Inner Sphere market in 3013, representing the latest evolution of that long lineage. Earthwerks marketed it as the definitive utility hover vehicle, emphasizing its compatibility with the established Freedom service and parts network that had accumulated across centuries of production. By the time of the Freedom 900's introduction, Earthwerks had built a global distribution and service infrastructure that smaller competitors found nearly impossible to match, allowing the company to maintain its market position even as rival manufacturers attempted to offer nominally superior alternatives.

Earthwerks' dominance of the Freedom series market has not been without controversy. Smaller manufacturers attempting to enter the hover utility segment repeatedly accused Earthwerks of using its scale to maintain artificially low pricing that undercut competitors before they could establish market footholds. Additional claims alleged that Earthwerks evaded import duties on vehicles assembled using low-cost labor from Capellan Confederation and Draconis Combine factories, undercutting domestic producers on worlds outside those states. No proof of deliberate anti-competitive conduct was ever established in any formal investigation, and Earthwerks consistently denied the allegations. Industry observers noted that the company's sheer manufacturing scale and accumulated infrastructure advantages were sufficient to explain its pricing without requiring any improper conduct.

By the late Dark Age era, rumors circulated in the civilian vehicle industry of an unannounced successor model, tentatively referred to as the Freedom 1000. Analysts speculated it would incorporate more advanced materials and systems, with improved performance over the Freedom 900. Earthwerks declined to confirm or deny the development, and some industry voices cautioned that building a more sophisticated vehicle risked alienating the vast market of underdeveloped worlds where the Freedom 900's simplicity was its most valued attribute.

text.deployment: The updated configuration, with light machine guns, Advanced Fire Control, and rear mine dispensers, became the definitive production standard in 3065 and the version most closely associated with the Fulmar's operational reputation. Ulysses Navy squadrons employed it in active patrol and convoy escort, using the mine dispenser capability to interdict coastal approaches and deny pirates the shallow-water transit routes they had previously exploited freely. The type's cargo capacity, sufficient for a full company of marines and their equipment, was demonstrated during the Penelope island assault and has been replicated in subsequent operations across the Federated Suns. The Fulmar has also attracted criminal users: smugglers recognized that the design's speed, amphibious capability, and military-grade sensors made it valuable for exactly the operations that naval patrols were trying to prevent.

The initial Fulmar configuration entered service with the Ulysses Navy in 3056, replacing improvised armed Cormorants in convoy escort duties along the planet's major shipping lanes. The standard machine gun armament proved adequate against lightly armed pirate craft in most engagements, though crews identified limited accuracy against fast-moving targets as a meaningful constraint. The Original configuration remained in production only until the updated variant superseded it, and most units were subsequently upgraded or replaced rather than retained in their initial form. Small numbers served in patrol roles on other ocean-dominated worlds in the Federated Suns during the transition period.

text.overview: The Galaport Ground Tug Trailer is an unpowered tracked cargo carrier designed to be towed by the Galaport Ground Tug in heavy-haul DropPort operations. Matching the tug in both mass and general dimensions, the trailer is built to accept the largest standard cargo containers and bulk freight packages that DropShip logistics require. Together, a single tug and trailer combination can move nearly five hundred tons of cargo in one pass, a capacity that made the Galaport system a benchmark for DropPort logistics when it entered service alongside the tug in 2457. Like the tug itself, the trailer design has seen little fundamental change across the centuries since its introduction, defined by the simplicity and robustness that demanding industrial use requires.
text.capabilities:
The Galaport Ground Tug Trailer is a purely passive cargo platform, carrying no engine, weapons, or active electronic systems. Its eighty-eight-ton standard cargo hold can accommodate most forms of containerized freight and bulk materials, with loading access provided by twin side doors, one on each flank. Environmental sealing protects cargo from atmospheric hazards common to active DropPort environments, including fuel vapor, exhaust gases, and particulate contamination from landing thrust.

The trailer incorporates both tractor and trailer chassis modifications, allowing it to be towed by the Galaport Ground Tug while also serving as a lead unit in an extended train with additional trailers coupled behind. This chaining capability allows a single tug to haul multiple trailers on routes with adequate clearance. The trailer's commercial-grade armor plating matches the BAR 6 standard of the tug, providing adequate protection for tarmac operations. The lack of any propulsion system is the trailer's principal limitation, rendering it entirely dependent on the tug for movement and positioning.
text.deployment: The Galaport Ground Tug Trailer operates exclusively in tandem with the Galaport Ground Tug or comparable tractor vehicles. It is most commonly deployed at major DropPorts handling heavy interstellar freight, where its substantial cargo capacity and environmental sealing justify its size. Trailers are typically staged in dedicated marshaling areas and coupled to tugs as needed for individual cargo runs, allowing a small tug fleet to serve a much larger trailer pool through flexible rotation. Specialized trailer variants, including refueling versions fitted with insulated reaction mass tanks, exist alongside the standard cargo configuration for facilities requiring dedicated propellant transfer operations.
text.battleHistory:
The Galaport Ground Tug Trailer was developed concurrently with the ground tug itself, the two forming an integrated logistics system from the outset. While the tug provided the motive force, the trailer's design prioritized maximum cargo acceptance in minimum unit count. Long trains of lighter vehicles, typical of planetary airstrips, were judged too unwieldy for the tight approaches between DropShip pits at a facility the scale of Galaport. A single tug-trailer combination could accomplish what dozens of lighter vehicles would struggle to manage safely in the chaotic environment of an active DropPort landing field.

Trailer operations at Galaport declined alongside tug operations when mercenary traffic shifted to Outreach in the 3040s. Much of the trailer fleet entered long-term storage or was sold offworld, leaving the once-busy marshaling yards largely empty. The Jihad's destruction of Outreach brought renewed demand for both tugs and trailers, with the surviving fleet returned to service. Discussions of new trailer construction accompanied the broader push to expand Galaport's capacity to handle the resurgent mercenary trade, and the basic trailer design was considered sound enough to reproduce without modification.

text.overview: The Galaport Ground Tug is a massive tracked support vehicle designed for heavy cargo operations at major DropPorts throughout the Inner Sphere. Originally built to serve the enormous Galaport facility outside Galatea City on Galatea, the design dates to 2457 and has remained essentially unchanged for centuries. The tug's primary purpose is hauling cargo trailers across the ferrocrete expanses of busy DropShip landing fields, moving supplies, equipment, and reaction mass between storage areas and grounded vessels. Versions of the design, ranging from modest luggage carts to true behemoths, operate on virtually every inhabited world in the Inner Sphere. The Galaport variant, built to handle the extreme demands of one of the Inner Sphere's busiest DropPorts, represents the high end of the type: a 200-ton fusion-powered crawler capable of moving freight loads that would challenge dedicated military logistics units.
text.capabilities:
Powered by a fusion engine and moving on wide tracked drives, the Galaport Ground Tug achieves a modest cruise speed of roughly twelve kilometers per hour and a flank speed approaching eighteen. This deliberate pace is adequate for DropPort work, where precision matters more than speed. The hull is protected by commercial-grade plating sufficient to withstand the hazards of active tarmac operations, including debris strikes, proximity to landing thrust, and minor vehicle collisions. Environmental sealing protects the three-person crew from exhaust gases, dust clouds, and other atmospheric hazards endemic to busy landing facilities.

A tractor chassis modification allows the tug to couple with and haul the paired ground trailer. A forward-mounted searchlight provides illumination for operations in poor visibility, including the dense dust clouds raised by landing or departing DropShips. The vehicle carries no weapons and relies on commercial communications and navigation systems suited to its logistics mission rather than military-grade electronics. The absence of a turret and any armament is a deliberate trade-off, freeing mass for the structural and mechanical systems required to haul enormous cargo loads reliably over thousands of operational hours.
text.deployment: The Galaport Ground Tug operates primarily at major DropPorts and spaceport facilities throughout the Inner Sphere. In standard DropPort operations, the tug pairs with one or more cargo trailers to haul freight between DropShips and storage facilities. The vehicle's environmental sealing and commercial durability make it suitable for operations on worlds with hostile atmospheric conditions, and its size allows it to work alongside even the largest DropShip classes. Outside of DropPort contexts, similar vehicles serve military logistics bases, supply depots, and large manufacturing facilities where bulk cargo movement over short distances is a regular requirement.
text.battleHistory:
The Galaport Ground Tug originated on Galatea during the Age of War, developed to meet the logistical demands of the massive Galaport DropPort complex outside Galatea City. As one of the largest DropPorts in the Inner Sphere, Galaport required industrial vehicles capable of handling the constant flow of cargo serving hundreds of simultaneously grounded DropShips. The drivers' unions that operated the crawlers took fierce pride in their work, claiming their vehicles moved more material than most standing armies, a boast that was difficult to dispute given the volume of traffic through Galaport at its peak.

The rise of Outreach as the premier mercenary hub of the Inner Sphere in the 3040s devastated the Galaport economy and with it the market for ground tugs. Most of the Galaport crawler fleet was scrapped or transferred offworld as mercenary traffic dwindled to a fraction of its former volume. A small number of tugs remained operational on the increasingly quiet ferrocrete fields, operated by skeleton crews waiting for business that rarely came. Those operators who maintained their equipment through the lean years developed an intimate familiarity with the vehicles that newer operators lacked.

The destruction of Outreach during the Jihad revived Galatea's fortunes and with them the demand for ground tugs. Mercenary traffic began returning to Galaport, and the surviving crawler operators found themselves well-positioned to capitalize on renewed demand. Unions pressed for expanded budgets to construct additional crawlers to handle the growing volume, and the long-dormant fleet gradually returned to full operational tempo. Throughout these changes, the fundamental design of the Galaport Ground Tug remained constant, a practical acknowledgment that a machine this well-suited to its purpose required no reinvention.

text.deployment: The Command Post configuration equips the GESV tractor with seven tons of communication equipment and two Remote Sensor Dispensers, transforming the vehicle into a mobile headquarters. Requiring a nine-person crew, this configuration is deployed with command-level units at the company, battalion, and regimental echelons to provide flexible communications infrastructure in the field. Its mobility allows command elements to reposition frequently, reducing vulnerability to counter-battery fire and enemy intelligence targeting.

The Field Kitchen configuration mounts two field kitchens alongside refrigerated and standard cargo to support sustained field operations. With an expanded kitchen crew of eight, the configuration feeds upward of 300 personnel per service. It is deployed primarily with large rear-echelon formations, refugee operations, and disaster relief missions where providing hot meals across a broad population is a significant morale and operational factor.

The MASH configuration equips the GESV with a full MASH unit and six surgical theaters, supported by a medical complement of 36 personnel. It provides organic surgical capability to formations operating beyond the range of fixed medical facilities. The configuration is deployed immediately behind front-line units to minimize patient transit time, and is frequently paired with GESV Trailer bunk configurations to expand patient housing capacity.

The Bunk configuration provides mobile living quarters for infantry and other personnel operating in field environments. Two foot infantry bays accommodate up to sixty people, with a small cargo allowance for basic personal supplies. Conditions are acknowledged as cramped, but most soldiers find the configuration preferable to sleeping in the open. It is most commonly paired with a GESV tractor running the MASH or Command Post configuration, where the need to house significant numbers of assigned personnel makes dedicated bunk space operationally valuable.

The Cargo configuration maximizes available interior space for general logistics transport, with a capacity of up to eleven and a half tons. The flexible interior can also serve as a workspace for intelligence personnel, staff officers, or technical specialists requiring office space in the field. It is the most versatile of the trailer configurations and is frequently deployed with any of the tractor configurations depending on the current operational requirement.

text.overview: The Gienah-DuraPaq Elite Series 3 is a heavy tracked land train tractor produced through a joint venture between Lyran Commonwealth-based Gienah Automotive and Free Worlds League foodstuffs manufacturer DuraPaq Solutions. First produced in 2899, the Elite Series 3 was designed to address a fundamental logistical challenge on colony worlds and undeveloped planets: the need to move large quantities of cargo across vast distances where roads, railways, and waterways do not exist. Capable of hauling a convoy of tracked trailer modules, the tractor became one of the most commercially successful civilian ground transport platforms in the Inner Sphere, achieving market dominance that competitors from House Davion and House Kurita have found difficult to challenge. Its reputation for sustained reliability in harsh operating conditions cemented the design's position for over a century after its introduction.
text.capabilities:
The Elite Series 3 tractor is built around a tractor chassis modification enabling it to pull multiple trailer modules across difficult terrain. The 200-ton vehicle is powered by a fusion engine, providing effectively unlimited operational range compared to conventional fuel-burning alternatives. Cruise speed is modest at 30 km/h, with a maximum of 50 km/h. These figures reflect a design philosophy that prioritizes sustained long-haul capacity and durability over transit speed. The trade-off is significant: the Elite Series 3 is not a rapid-response transport, and any mission requiring time-sensitive delivery across hostile terrain will quickly expose its limitations.

The tractor's crew complement of three enlisted personnel operates and maintains the vehicle. Crew quarters for four and a four-person medical bay are built into the cab, supporting the extended overland journeys these vehicles routinely undertake. A three-ton integrated lift hoist handles loading and securing cargo into the trailer modules. Six tons of BAR 6 commercial armor provides basic protection against wilderness hazards and minor criminal threats. The tractor carries no weapons, a deliberate choice that keeps the design focused on cargo capacity but leaves it dependent on escorts in any environment where organized threats are likely.
text.deployment: The Elite Series 3 tractor operates across a wide range of civilian freight routes, primarily on colony worlds and underdeveloped planets where conventional transportation infrastructure is absent or impractical. Configured with crew quarters and a medical bay as standard, it serves long-haul overland missions spanning hundreds of kilometers between frontier settlements. The design is marketed and sold across both Lyran and League space, and is found in smaller numbers throughout the wider Inner Sphere. Dozens of derivative configurations exist across multiple worlds and regional manufacturers, though the Gienah-DuraPaq lines on Gienah remain the recognized standard for quality and reliability.
text.battleHistory:
The Elite Series 3's origins trace to a corporate negotiation conducted against a backdrop of interstellar war. Gienah Automotive had long maintained trade relationships across the border with Free Worlds League customers, an unusual arrangement for a Lyran company. In 2864, as the leaders of the five Great Houses met on New Earth for peace talks at the close of the Second Succession War, DuraPaq Solutions CEO Earl Jarv Kefalczyk approached Gienah Automotive's Duke Solia Zdenekova with a proposal to combine DuraPaq's packaging and logistics expertise with Gienah's manufacturing capability.

Negotiations continued through the opening years of the Third Succession War, slowed but not ended by renewed fighting. By the late twenty-ninth century, the two companies had established Gienah-DuraPaq as a joint operation on Gienah, and the first Elite Series 3 land trains entered production in 2899. The design supplied colony worlds across both realms, filling a transport gap that neither House's military logistics network was equipped to address commercially.

The Elite Series 3 quickly established dominance over rival designs. The Davion-produced O'Keefre Model II and Kurita's Isesaki Roku Royal both competed for similar markets, but the Gienah-DuraPaq product's consistent quality and its unique cross-border availability gave it a reach neither competitor could match. By 3067, Gienah Automotive had expanded to three factories on Gienah, and the land train line remained central to its civilian production portfolio. A September 3048 raid by the Third Free Worlds Legionnaires and Second Fusiliers of Oriente on Gienah resulted in the theft of vehicles and schematics from the Combat Vehicles factory, though the Gienah-DuraPaq civilian production campus continued normal operations.

The Jihad era brought additional pressure to the company. Gienah Automotive attempted a post-Jihad stock offering to fund re-entry into the defense market, but the sale fell short of its targets, and the company remained focused on civilian production into the Dark Age. By the time Clan Wolf Empire asserted control over Gienah, the joint venture that had bridged two rival Great Houses for over a century found itself operating under a wholly different political authority.

text.overview: The Gienah-DuraPaq Elite Series 3T is the trailer module complement to the Elite Series 3 land train tractor. Produced by the same Gienah-DuraPaq joint venture on Gienah, the 50-ton module is an unpowered unit designed to be towed by the Series 3 tractor across colony worlds and frontier territories lacking transportation infrastructure. Multiple trailer modules can be coupled behind a single tractor, providing scalable cargo capacity for a given mission. The Series 3T is manufactured in four standard configurations covering dry cargo, refrigerated goods, liquid freight, and livestock transport. This modular approach gave the Elite Series 3 system a versatility that regional competitors largely lacked, and it contributed significantly to the design's commercial success across both the Lyran Commonwealth and the Free Worlds League.
text.capabilities:
The Series 3T trailer has no propulsion system of its own, relying entirely on the Series 3 tractor for movement. It is built on a tracked medium chassis incorporating tractor and trailer chassis modification controls to facilitate coupling. The standard dry goods configuration carries 39 tons of cargo, accessible through four doors, one per side. The refrigerated variant reduces capacity to 33.9 tons to accommodate cooling equipment, making it suitable for perishable goods transport. The liquid cargo version carries 35.4 tons of fluid freight, while the livestock configuration supports up to 31.9 tons of live animals with appropriate ventilation.

Three tons of BAR 3 commercial armor provides physical resilience against the hazards of wilderness travel. The lighter protection compared to the tractor reflects the trailer's passive role. No crew is assigned to the module, with all loading and securing operations performed by the tractor crew using the tractor's integrated lift hoist. The lack of weapons or active systems makes the trailer entirely dependent on the tractor and any escort elements for security in contested areas.
text.deployment: The Series 3T trailer is deployed wherever the Elite Series 3 tractor operates, typically in trains of two to six modules depending on terrain and mission requirements. Standard cargo modules are most common, used for general freight between frontier settlements. Refrigerated and liquid cargo variants are found on agricultural worlds where food preservation and bulk liquid transport support the local economy. The livestock configuration sees use on ranching worlds and early-stage colony planets. Individual trailer modules are also maintained as stationary storage units at remote sites between transit cycles, a secondary use case that further extended the design's commercial appeal.
text.battleHistory:
The Series 3T trailer module was conceived alongside the Series 3 tractor as an integral part of the Gienah-DuraPaq land train system. From the outset, the modular trailer design was central to the product's commercial proposition, allowing customers to acquire a single tractor and multiple specialized modules rather than separate vehicles for each cargo type. This flexibility proved commercially valuable, particularly on colony worlds where capital for equipment purchases was limited and operational needs varied widely across seasons and economic cycles.

The modular approach also offered practical maintenance advantages in frontier operations. A damaged trailer module could be exchanged at any equipped facility without requiring replacement of the tractor, reducing overall operating costs and improving system availability in environments where full service depots were rare. These qualities reinforced the Elite Series 3 system's reputation for reliability and contributed to its sustained market position against competing land train designs from House Davion and House Kurita throughout the Succession Wars period.

The trailer module line continued production in parallel with the tractor throughout the Gienah-DuraPaq venture's operational history. As Gienah changed hands politically, passing from Lyran Commonwealth control through the Federated Commonwealth period and ultimately into the Clan Wolf Empire's territory, the civilian production campus on Gienah maintained output. The Series 3T remained in wide use across the Inner Sphere long after its 2899 introduction, reflection of the durability of the original design concept.

text.overview: The Harpoon ParaSub was initially commissioned on the water-rich Capellan world of Principia by the mercenary command Kraken Unleashed. It is an unpressurized submersible which moves five troopers and supplies them with weapon support. Since its debut it has become available for sale on the open market, enabling the creation of submersible mechanized infantry for any interested buyer.

When AFFS motorized infantry commanders expressed dissatisfaction with improvised transport solutions, Pintel Corporation responded with a purpose-built answer. Introduced in 3001, the PVC-141 Heavy Combat ATV was designed from the outset around infantry needs rather than adapted from a civilian platform. The vehicle earned early appreciation from frontline NCOs for its unusual versatility, combining genuine all-terrain performance, modest cargo capacity, and the ability to mount a crew-served support weapon on a single compact platform.

Lacking integral weapons, the ATV depends on flexibility and mobility rather than firepower. It has carved out a consistent role across AFFS motorized infantry formations as a personal transport, supply courier, and light command vehicle, valued for practical reliability rather than any particular tactical distinction.
text.capabilities:
The Heavy Combat ATV is a compact wheeled support vehicle built around operational flexibility rather than combat power. Its ICE powerplant, running on petrochemicals or substitute fuels with no modification required, delivers a cruise speed of roughly 34 kilometers per hour and a top speed near 65 kilometers per hour, adequate for keeping pace with motorized infantry formations across most terrain types.

The vehicle's most notable engineering feature is its chassis. Oversized wheels combined with off-road and tractor chassis and controls modifications allow the ATV to negotiate terrain that would stop conventional light vehicles, including water crossings through full amphibious capability. This cross-terrain performance is the defining tactical strength of the design.

Protection is minimal: a Barrier Armor Rating of 2 provides little more than fragmentation cover, and the ATV carries no integral weapons. Its Pintle Mount accepts any support weapon up to 22 kilograms, giving crews mission-specific flexibility without committing the vehicle to a fixed armament. Seating accommodates the driver and one passenger, with a rear cargo bay handling 145 kilograms of supplies and equipment. A rear hitch allows the vehicle to tow a small trailer when resupply demands exceed the onboard capacity.
text.deployment:
The Heavy Combat ATV serves in AFFS motorized infantry formations across the Federated Suns, typically assigned in pairs per infantry section as personal transports and supply carriers. Its amphibious capability makes it particularly valued in the Draconis and Capellan March theatres, where river crossings and coastal operations are common and light vehicle availability is often limited.

Platoon commanders frequently equip the Pintle Mount with a machine gun or light grenade launcher depending on local supply conditions, and the mount's wide compatibility means considerable variation in practice across different formations. Some examples serve in logistics and command liaison roles behind the forward line, where the vehicle's ability to refuel from non-standard sources proves useful in austere operating environments far from established supply depots.
text.battleHistory:
Prior to the PVC-141's introduction, AFFS motorized infantry units typically relied on whatever commercial or surplus vehicles their commanders could procure. Motorcycles, civilian ATVs, and light utility vehicles were common, offering mobility but rarely the combined qualities of cross-terrain performance, cargo capacity, and weapon-mounting capability that infantry platoon commanders wanted in a single platform. Field modifications were common but inconsistent, and logistical support for such improvised fleets was a persistent challenge.

Pintel Corporation addressed these complaints directly. Working from feedback gathered from AFFS motorized infantry NCOs and logistics officers, the company's design team built a vehicle intended to replace the patchwork of improvised solutions with a purpose-designed platform. The PVC-141 entered service in 3001 under the AFFS designation Heavy Combat ATV, and its reception among frontline motorized infantry was broadly positive. The all-terrain wheel configuration and amphibious capability allowed platoons to operate across environments that previously required attached engineering support, and the standardized Pintle Mount gave platoon leaders a reliable means of integrating squad-level support weapons into vehicle-mounted operations.

The factory producing the PVC-141 has not been publicly documented. Pintel Corporation's manufacturing infrastructure has been difficult to trace in open records, and the production facility for the Heavy Combat ATV has never been confirmed in available reporting. Despite this, the vehicle achieved consistent distribution across AFFS motorized infantry formations, suggesting Pintel maintained reliable output through the Succession Wars and into the early Dark Age. The ATV continues to serve wherever AFFS ground forces operate, enduring as a practical solution to an enduring infantry logistics problem.

text.overview: The Hector Road Train Tractor is a 160-ton wheeled heavy transport vehicle introduced in 2500 to address a persistent logistics gap on worlds without adequate rail networks, where air freight and DropShip transport are prohibitively costly for bulk shipments. The Irian-built Hector serves as the prime mover of the Irian Road Train system, capable of hauling 150 tons of cargo or more across distances up to 2,500 kilometers. Built for multi-day overland runs without external support infrastructure, the tractor includes crew accommodations for two off-duty drivers, a kitchenette, and a miniature bathroom, allowing crews to rotate and maintain continuous movement. The Hector became a recognizable presence across the Free Worlds League and found use throughout the Inner Sphere, valued as a dependable logistics backbone for worlds that commercial trucking made accessible where rail did not reach.
text.capabilities:
Powered by an internal combustion engine, the Hector Tractor achieves a cruise speed of four movement points and a flank speed of six, with a 2,500-kilometer fuel range suited to the long overland hauls that define its role. Its wheeled propulsion system optimizes fuel efficiency on improved roads and prepared surfaces, though the large footprint of the 160-ton vehicle limits it to favorable terrain. The tractor carries 12 tons of cargo in its own compartment, supplemented by whatever trailer modules it tows. BAR 3 armor provides coverage appropriate for a civilian vehicle, offering basic protection against minor hazards rather than battlefield threats. The Hector has no weapons and is not intended for combat operations.

The tractor operates at full capacity when running independently, but performance degrades when pulling trailer modules, as documented in the operator manuals. Experienced operators plan routes and loads accordingly, typically limiting trailer combinations to two modules on flat terrain and to a single trailer where grades or poor road conditions are a factor. The built-in driver accommodations support continuous 24-hour operations: off-duty drivers rest while the vehicle moves, allowing the train to cover distances that would require multiple-day layovers under normal commercial trucking arrangements. Standard equipment fitments include an IR camera for low-visibility navigation and a lift hoist for cargo handling at destinations without dedicated unloading infrastructure.
text.deployment: The Hector Road Train Tractor operates across the Free Worlds League and numerous Inner Sphere states as a commercial long-haul transport vehicle, typically assigned to planetary logistics contractors, government freight operations, and independent transport cooperatives. The tractor may run independently for short-haul or light cargo missions, or couple with one or two trailer modules for extended bulk operations. Performance degrades progressively with each additional trailer, and operators on difficult terrain typically limit loads to a single module. Crews of three manage extended multi-day operations using the built-in driver accommodations. The IR camera and lift hoist support independent cargo handling at destinations without dedicated unloading infrastructure.
text.battleHistory:
Irian manufacturers developed the Hector Road Train system in 2500 to address a structural gap in planetary logistics. On worlds without developed rail networks, bulk freight moved slowly and expensively. Air cargo and DropShip freight handled high-value goods, but agricultural commodities, raw materials, and manufactured goods required a ground transport solution that could match rail volume capacity at a fraction of the capital cost. Road trains offered that solution, and the Hector became among the most widely recognized implementations of the concept in the Free Worlds League.

The Irian design distinguished itself through practical crew amenities. Earlier road train designs required relay crews and overnight stops at way stations, introducing logistical complexity and schedule uncertainty. Irian's engineering team incorporated driver accommodations directly into the tractor unit, allowing a three-person crew to rotate through driving shifts continuously. The result was a vehicle that could sustain four days of uninterrupted travel before delivering its cargo, covering distances that competing designs managed only through elaborate support infrastructure. This capability proved especially valuable on frontier worlds where way stations were sparse or nonexistent.

The Hector spread through the Free Worlds League and into neighboring states through licensing and commercial export. Its civilian character insulated it from the worst effects of the Succession Wars: while military vehicles were destroyed or stripped for parts, commercial road trains continued to haul cargo, wear out through normal use, and be repaired by local workshops. The simplicity of the ICE-powered drivetrain and the availability of common wheeled vehicle components meant that maintenance could be performed far from any major manufacturing center.

By the Late Succession Wars, Hector tractors in various states of modification remained operational on dozens of worlds. Some units had been in continuous service for over a century, rebuilt repeatedly with locally sourced components. The design's endurance became its own form of legacy, a sign of the soundness of the original 2500 engineering. The Hector continued in service through the Clan Invasion era and into the Dark Age largely unchanged, as operators found little reason to replace a working vehicle when access to more sophisticated alternatives remained uncertain.
text.notes: Unit is 1 ton over weight, removed 1 ton of Cargo to make legal.

text.deployment: The standard cargo configuration carries 67 tons of dry bulk goods and represents the general-purpose variant of the Hector trailer system. Four side access doors facilitate loading and unloading with standard freight handling equipment. The configuration is deployed widely across Free Worlds League agricultural and industrial operations, moving grain, packaged goods, construction materials, and manufactured freight. It operates as the default trailer for Hector Road Train combinations where cargo is not specialized, and is commonly mixed with other configurations in multi-trailer trains.

The liquid cargo configuration carries 60.5 tons of fluid freight in a sealed tank system, suited to fuels, agricultural chemicals, bulk water, and liquid food products. Four access doors facilitate connection to pumping equipment at loading and destination points. The configuration is deployed on Free Worlds League worlds with significant fuel, chemical, or liquid agricultural freight needs, commonly operating in industrial corridors and around DropPort fuel distribution networks.

The livestock configuration accommodates 55.5 tons of live animals in transport housing appropriate for commercial livestock movement. Four access doors support loading and unloading at farms, markets, and processing facilities. The configuration is deployed extensively in Free Worlds League agricultural regions where livestock transport between production, processing, and market destinations forms a substantial portion of planetary commercial traffic. It is commonly operated in mixed trains alongside standard cargo modules.

The passenger module configuration supports up to 308 passengers across eleven infantry compartments, with three field kitchens and five tons of standard cargo space for luggage and freight. Three doors on the left, right, and rear provide boarding and egress access. The configuration is deployed on frontier and developing worlds as a substitute for absent rail passenger service, operating on scheduled commercial routes and under government transit contracts. Military logistics commands employ the passenger module for troop movement and dependent transport during peacetime rotation cycles, taking advantage of its large capacity and independence from fixed transit infrastructure.

The refrigerated cargo configuration carries 58 tons of temperature-sensitive freight using active cooling systems, suited to perishable food products, pharmaceuticals, and other cold chain cargo. Four access doors accommodate standard freight handling at temperature-controlled loading and unloading facilities. The configuration is deployed in food distribution networks, pharmaceutical supply chains, and fresh produce logistics across the Free Worlds League, operating on time-sensitive routes connecting agricultural production worlds to urban markets and DropPort cold storage facilities.

text.capabilities:
The Hesiod's most significant technical feature is its OmniVehicle chassis, which provides three tons of OmniPod space for swapping between four distinct working modules. The 7-ton frame rides on an off-road wheeled chassis that handles unpaved terrain reliably, though the vehicle is not intended for high-speed operation. Its ICE engine delivers a cruise speed of 40 km/h and a top speed of 60 km/h, drawing on a 2,666 km range from its alcohol fuel supply. That extended range allows the vehicle to operate independently of fuel logistics for extended periods, a practical necessity on frontier worlds.

All configurations carry commercial armor at BAR 4, offering environmental protection against the elements but minimal resistance to deliberate weapons fire. The Hesiod is unarmed in its baseline configurations, and its crew of two enlisted operators shares the cab regardless of which module is installed.

The vehicle's principal limitation is its single-configuration operation. Swapping OmniPods requires ground crew support and downtime, meaning the flexibility advantage of the platform is realized across a deployment rather than moment to moment. Operators who expect to reconfigure frequently will need logistics support unavailable in austere frontier conditions. The light construction also limits the Hesiod to civilian workloads - it is not suited to heavy-duty operations alongside large construction equipment.
text.deployment: The Harvester configuration mounts a front combine alongside half a ton of rear cargo space, optimized for small-scale crop collection. It is a common sight working in support of larger harvesting operations on developing worlds, handling lower-density plantings where larger dedicated harvesters would be impractical. The retained cargo space allows operators to stage harvested material for transfer without requiring an additional vehicle, extending the configuration's utility in resource-constrained colonial environments.

text.capabilities:
The Hesiod's most significant technical feature is its OmniVehicle chassis, which provides three tons of OmniPod space for swapping between four distinct working modules. The 7-ton frame rides on an off-road wheeled chassis that handles unpaved terrain reliably, though the vehicle is not intended for high-speed operation. Its ICE engine delivers a cruise speed of 40 km/h and a top speed of 60 km/h, drawing on a 2,666 km range from its alcohol fuel supply. That extended range allows the vehicle to operate independently of fuel logistics for extended periods, a practical necessity on frontier worlds.

All configurations carry commercial armor at BAR 4, offering environmental protection against the elements but minimal resistance to deliberate weapons fire. The Hesiod is unarmed in its baseline configurations, and its crew of two enlisted operators shares the cab regardless of which module is installed.

The vehicle's principal limitation is its single-configuration operation. Swapping OmniPods requires ground crew support and downtime, meaning the flexibility advantage of the platform is realized across a deployment rather than moment to moment. Operators who expect to reconfigure frequently will need logistics support unavailable in austere frontier conditions. The light construction also limits the Hesiod to civilian workloads, it is not suited to heavy-duty operations alongside large construction equipment.
text.deployment: The Bulldozer configuration replaces the cargo module with a blade suited for earthmoving, land clearing, and terrain preparation. One ton of cargo is retained for tools and materials. The Hesiod's off-road chassis is an asset in this role, allowing operation across raw ground ahead of settlement infrastructure. This configuration is most common during the early phases of colonial development, clearing land for planting, construction access, and drainage work before heavier specialized equipment arrives.

The Crane configuration mounts a front lift hoist in place of the cargo bay, suited for placement and retrieval tasks at height. It supports construction and maintenance operations on colonial settlements, handling prefabricated structural components, equipment positioning, and oversized loads too heavy for manual handling. The rear door is retained, allowing secondary load-carrying in situations where hoist operations and cargo transport are needed during the same work cycle.

The Prime configuration carries three tons of standard cargo accessed via a rear-loading door. It is the most broadly deployed of the Hesiod's modules, serving logistics and supply functions on agricultural settlements, construction sites, and frontier colonies. Its general-purpose nature makes it the default configuration for operators who require flexible light transport rather than a specialized tool, and it is frequently paired with other Hesiod configurations to cover material-handling needs between specialized operations.

text.overview: The HMRV DeConAid Trailer is an environmentally sealed medical support trailer produced by Brown-Corning, Limited on Caph as part of the expanded Oppie system introduced in 3068. Not technically a production variant of the Oppie tractor, the DeConAid is a distinct trailer type that became a common sight on Word of Blake Protectorate worlds wherever NBC contamination required both recovery and medical response. Classified as a mobile MASH unit, the trailer provides field surgical capability to personnel operating in contaminated environments where conventional medical facilities are inaccessible or compromised. Its environmental sealing allows medical staff to treat casualties without requiring full decontamination of the patient before entry.
text.capabilities:
The DeConAid Trailer houses eleven medical theaters within its sealed interior, allowing simultaneous treatment of multiple casualties. Six searchlights support operations in low-visibility conditions, and two sprayers enable decontamination of personnel and equipment at the trailer access points before entry. A fully sealed five-ton infantry bay carries medical staff who can accompany the trailer into hazardous zones. Twenty tons of liquid storage provide capacity for medical fluids, decontaminants, and water.

Like the Salvage Bed, the DeConAid carries no engine and depends entirely on a towing vehicle for mobility. The trailer's medium-rated chassis uses environmental sealing throughout rather than additional armor, prioritizing crew protection from contamination over ballistic threats. The design is not intended for direct combat zones, and medical teams typically position the DeConAid in protected areas while the Oppie tractor conducts forward recovery operations. Mobility depends entirely on the availability and condition of the prime mover.
text.deployment: Distributed widely across Word of Blake Protectorate worlds during the Jihad, the DeConAid Trailer typically operates towed by an O-66 "Oppie" tractor or other suitable heavy vehicle. Medical teams position it in protected areas near NBC cleanup operations, using the sealed interior to treat casualties without requiring full decontamination before entry. The DeConAid's presence alongside Oppie tractors was one of the more visible signs of Blakist investment in Protectorate world rehabilitation.
text.battleHistory:
The HMRV DeConAid Trailer was developed as part of the expanded Oppie system that Brown-Corning, Limited introduced in 3068 following the company's revival under Word of Blake support on Caph. Unlike the Salvage Bed, which entered service alongside the O-65 in 2822, the DeConAid is a product of the post-revival production run, representing a new capability added when the Blakists encouraged expanded product development beyond the original blueprints.

The Blakist interest in NBC cleanup capabilities on Protectorate worlds drove demand for the DeConAid from its initial production run. Word of Blake logistics units distributed the trailers across Protectorate worlds alongside newly produced O-66 tractors, giving cleanup teams an integrated medical response capability. The combination of environmental sealing and eleven surgical theaters filled a recognized gap in the support vehicle inventory that existing MASH equipment could not address in contaminated environments.

text.overview: The HMRV Salvage Bed is a towed recovery trailer designed to operate in conjunction with the O-66 "Oppie" tractor unit. Produced by Brown-Corning, Limited at the same Caph facility as the tractor, the Salvage Bed entered service in 2822 alongside the original O-65. Its defining feature is a universal trailer hookup that allows attachment to the Oppie tractor or a wide variety of other heavy vehicles and construction equipment, giving recovery teams flexibility when dedicated tractors are unavailable. The Salvage Bed functions as a working platform and load carrier, extending the Oppie system's total recovery capacity and providing additional specialized equipment for sustained salvage operations in NBC-contaminated environments.
text.capabilities:
The Salvage Bed carries two lift hoists for raising heavy wreckage from unstable positions, a backhoe for earthmoving support, and five searchlights for illuminating work areas in degraded visibility. Twenty tons of liquid storage provide capacity for decontaminants, water, or other operational fluids. The universal trailer hookup is the design's most significant feature: it allows the Salvage Bed to be drawn by virtually any suitably rated heavy recovery vehicle, not only the dedicated Oppie tractor, making the trailer a versatile asset when tractor availability is limited.

The Salvage Bed carries no engine and relies entirely on its towing vehicle for mobility. This dependency is its principal limitation, as the trailer cannot reposition without a suitable prime mover. Recovery teams must account for towing vehicle availability and terrain conditions when planning operations. The trailer's medium-rated chassis provides adequate structural capacity for the loads typical of BattleMech and vehicle recovery work.
text.deployment: Deployed as a towed companion to the O-66 "Oppie" tractor in standard NBC salvage operations, though its universal trailer hookup allows pairing with other heavy recovery vehicles when dedicated tractors are unavailable. The Salvage Bed is found wherever Oppie tractors operate, extending overall system capacity and providing the lift hoist and backhoe capability that the tractor unit alone does not carry.
text.battleHistory:
The HMRV Salvage Bed entered production in 2822 alongside the O-65 tractor unit, sharing the same operational history as its companion vehicle. Brown-Corning, Limited produced the Salvage Bed as an integral component of the Oppie system rather than a standalone design, recognizing that the tractor's working equipment alone would not provide sufficient capacity for sustained recovery operations across contaminated zones.

When the Draconis Combine raid destroyed the Brown-Corning facility on Caph, Salvage Bed production ceased along with all other company manufacturing. Surviving trailers continued operating through the Succession Wars until attrition and parts shortages eliminated the fleet. Production resumed in 3068 when Brown-Corning restarted operations under Word of Blake support, and the Salvage Bed returned to service alongside the rebuilt O-66 tractor. The restored blueprints provided to company leadership covered the full Oppie system, ensuring the Salvage Bed returned to production without design gaps.

text.overview: The sealed Hoodling is a vehicle of extremely high quality that has been continuously manufactured on Terra since the twenty-ninth century. With its high speed, excellent communication and sensor suite, and comfortable crew accommodations, it is the premier covert operations vehicle for ComStar and its Explorer Corps. On a battlefield, there are few better eyes and ears than those of the Hoodling.

The tiny and relatively slow HoverPod is a very common tool for motorized and mechanized infantry units. These vehicles are very small and can easily be transported by most APCs. They award a high measure of individual mobility to troopers, but are in no way actual combat units, as their use requires a level of dexterity that precludes the deployment of support weaponry.

The Humming Bird is a search and rescue VTOL developed by Bermuda Combat Systems on Booker in 3074. Bermuda designed it for police and paramilitary organizations seeking an affordable platform capable of locating missing persons, downed pilots, and stranded personnel in hostile or remote environments. The vehicle's most noteworthy feature is its Bloodhound active probe, a piece of cutting-edge sensor technology that gives the Humming Bird detection capabilities rivaling dedicated military reconnaissance units. To offset the cost of these advanced sensors, Bermuda built the rest of the vehicle using deliberately primitive-level construction, keeping the price accessible to smaller government agencies and mercenary units. The resulting design attracted buyers well beyond its intended market, finding customers throughout the Magistracy of Canopus and across the Periphery.
text.capabilities:
The Humming Bird's chassis, engine, and armor are all constructed using primitive-level technology, a deliberate cost-reduction measure by Bermuda Combat Systems. The vehicle is a 30-ton VTOL powered by a fuel cell engine, capable of cruising at 75 km/h with a flank speed of 118 km/h and a fuel range of 2,456 kilometers. This speed advantage is the Humming Bird's primary defensive asset. The single ton of BAR 5 primitive armor protecting the hull offers minimal protection in any serious engagement, and crews are expected to avoid confrontation entirely, relying on altitude and evasion rather than fighting through contact.

The vehicle carries no weapons, reinforcing its non-combatant design intent. Its true value lies in its sensor package. The Bloodhound active probe provides exceptional detection range and can identify targets through cover and concealment that would defeat standard active probes. This capability makes the Humming Bird useful not only for rescue operations but also for reconnaissance, advance scouting, and threat assessment in uncertain environments.

Supporting its primary mission, the Humming Bird carries a lift hoist for extracting personnel or light equipment, and a mounted searchlight for night and low-visibility operations. Both systems are designed for easy removal, leaving the vehicle open to future weapon refits should buyers require a more combative configuration.
text.deployment: The Humming Bird (Rescue) serves primarily with Magistracy of Canopus police, paramilitary, and planetary militia forces, performing search and rescue, reconnaissance, and threat detection missions. Its general-production classification has placed it in service with mercenary commands throughout the Periphery, particularly those operating in contested or low-information environments where the Bloodhound active probe provides a meaningful intelligence advantage over locally available alternatives. The design's primitive systems and open modification framework have made it a popular base for local conversion, with many operators adding light weapons or supplemental cargo provisions. It is rarely deployed in front-line combat roles, typically operating behind friendly lines or in permissive environments where its minimal armor is not a critical liability.
text.battleHistory:
Bermuda Combat Systems introduced the Humming Bird in 3074, during the height of the Jihad. Police and paramilitary forces across the Periphery were in desperate need of capable and affordable equipment, and advanced sensor systems were typically out of reach for smaller agencies and planetary governments. Bermuda's engineers designed the Humming Bird to bridge that gap, pairing a Bloodhound active probe with an otherwise primitive construction to produce a vehicle that small organizations could actually afford to purchase and maintain.

The Magistracy of Canopus was the vehicle's primary early customer. Canopian police and rescue organizations ordered the majority of the first production run, deploying Humming Birds across border worlds and urban centers where their sensor capabilities could locate smugglers, insurgents, and accident victims with equal effectiveness. The vehicle's reputation spread quickly through mercenary networks and Periphery trading channels, and subsequent production runs found buyers well outside Canopian space.

Bermuda survived the Jihad without significant production disruption, continuing to supply the Humming Bird through the Dark Age and into the ilClan period. The vehicle's primitive construction, originally a concession to cost, proved an unexpected logistical advantage. Spare parts remained widely available, and field repairs could be performed by technicians without access to advanced manufacturing tools. This resilience helped cement the Humming Bird's place as a recognizable fixture in Periphery inventories across multiple generations of conflict and political change.

text.deployment: The standard Ibex RV serves across the Free Worlds League in agricultural, commercial, and light government roles. Rural settlers and farming operations use it as a primary transport and logistics vehicle. Urban markets have adopted it as a premium utility vehicle, with security firms and corporate fleets operating it alongside civilian buyers. Law enforcement agencies deploy it for rural patrol and perimeter security on outlying worlds.

The later Gauss variant serves in similar roles to its predecessor but is preferred by units operating in areas where longer engagement distances are expected. Its side-mounted King David light Gauss rifles provide improved accuracy over the earlier pintle-mounted configuration, making it marginally more effective against light armor. It sees use in both militia patrol units and private security forces across the League's member states.

The Militarized version equips Free Worlds League Militia garrison units, planetary police forces, and private security contractors requiring a light armed patrol vehicle. Typically deployed on frontier and low-intensity worlds where conventional combat vehicles would be excessive, it provides a credible deterrent against unorganized threats without requiring specialized crew training or maintenance infrastructure.

text.overview:
The Ina-du Swamp Skimmer is a civilian hover support vehicle produced by Hoyle Systems on Zdice, a world defined by the sprawling canal metropolis of Zaniz City. Introduced in 2870, the lightweight ten-ton design was purpose-built to navigate the city's dense network of narrow waterways, serving the taxi and courier trades that thrived among the millions of residents who depended on canal transport. Named from an ancient Cherokee word for snake, the vehicle's slim profile and high acceleration made it well-suited for threading the city's tighter water routes.

Over the generations the Ina-du became so closely associated with Zaniz City life that it eventually transcended its role as a working vehicle, becoming a cultural fixture celebrated in the biennial Extraordinaire Canal Contest racing circuit and a symbol of the city's commercial identity.
text.capabilities:
The Ina-du Swamp Skimmer is engineered for agility and efficiency in confined urban waterway environments. At ten tons, it achieves a flank speed of 14 movement points using its fuel cell powerplant, making it responsive and quick for a vehicle of its configuration. The fuel cell drive provides efficient operation across 740 kilometers on a single fuel load, well-suited to the continuous service demands of a working taxi fleet. The hoverskirt design allows transit across both open water and low-gradient wet terrain, giving operators flexibility along canal edges and shallow banks.

The vehicle carries only minimal armor rated to BAR 5 standards, sufficient against incidental collisions and waterway hazards but meaningless in any combat scenario. It mounts no weapons and carries no military-grade systems. This is by design, reflecting Hoyle Systems' purely commercial intent for the platform.

A precision electronic sensor suite linked to the primary rear steering vanes automatically adjusts small sections of the airskirt in real time, compensating for tight maneuvers and improving handling in the narrow passages typical of Zaniz City's canal grid. The system adds some maintenance complexity but is valued by operators for the gain in responsiveness. Standard configuration accommodates two crew and four passengers in a convertible seating arrangement, with 0.2 tons of cargo capacity available when the passenger layout is configured.
text.deployment:
The Ina-du Swamp Skimmer operates exclusively in the civilian sector and has never been adapted for military purposes. Its primary operational environment is the canal network of Zaniz City on Zdice, where Hoyle Systems has maintained uninterrupted production since its 2870 introduction. The vehicle is standard equipment across all three of the city's major taxi unions and is widely used for courier, freight, and passenger transport on the waterway grid.

Its lack of weapons, minimal armor, and passenger-focused configuration make it unsuitable for any role beyond civilian transport. Beyond its working life, the Ina-du also sees competitive use in the biennial Extraordinaire Canal Contest, where strict regulations require all participating vehicles to be drawn from active motor pool assets, ensuring the racing circuit remains a showcase for the production model rather than purpose-built machines.
text.battleHistory:
Hoyle Systems introduced the Ina-du in 2870 to address the growing transportation demands of Zaniz City, a sprawling metropolis of over ten million residents laced with a complex network of canals and waterways. The design entered service quickly, adopted across the three major taxi unions that controlled fares and routes on the city's water grid. Over the following decades Hoyle made few significant changes to the design, maintaining the three-man skimmer's basic configuration while updating internal systems incrementally to reflect available components.

The hoverskirt was overhauled in 2997, the most significant engineering change in the vehicle's history. The redesign improved the precision airskirt adjustment system and was well-received across the taxi fleets, providing a measurable gain in handling in the tightest sections of the canal grid.

Competition among the taxi unions for routes and fares grew increasingly contentious through the late twenty-ninth and early thirtieth centuries. By 2999, over four hundred accidents and incidents in a single year reflected how violent that competition had become. After three members of the DeWalt Group died in what union leadership described as accidents, representatives from all three unions met to address the crisis. Their first conference resolved little, but out of those talks emerged the concept of a formal, organized outlet for competition. Jonas Silt proposed the Extraordinaire Canal Contest, a high-speed racing circuit using existing motor pool vehicles on a complex water course through the city.

The first ECC was held in 3001 over three days, drawing over 300,000 spectators despite initial resistance from the Zaniz City council. The event proved a commercial and cultural success. The ECC Racing Board adopted biennial scheduling, revealing a new eighty-kilometer course for each contest. Recognizing the commercial opportunity, Hoyle Systems developed a customization line for the Ina-du to serve the growing aftermarket. The Zdice Custom Expo grew from this activity, drawing over half a million visitors by 3066 to view accessories and custom show skimmers.

text.overview: Johnston Industries' military hoverbike was initially manufactured for the company's own security force and for the AFFS, which utilizes it in its mechanized infantry elements. It differs from other hoverbikes only in its extremely sturdy, reinforced structure, which allows for the becoming popular use of higher-grade military armor, giving it durability unusual for a vehicle of its size.

text.deployment: The standard JI-50 is the baseline Jifty configuration, equipped with two lift hoists, a pair of light machine guns, and 19.5 tons of cargo capacity. It remains the most common variant in service, primarily deployed by the Federated Suns armed forces and Capellan units that captured examples during the early stages of the Jihad.

The JI-50 (Hoist) is a field modification that removes all weaponry in favor of a third lift hoist, increasing the vehicle's recovery capability at the expense of any self-defense. Cargo capacity is somewhat reduced to accommodate the additional equipment. This variant is preferred by units operating in secure rear areas where the additional lifting capacity outweighs the loss of the machine guns.
text.battleHistory:
Johnston Industries developed the Jifty at their New Syrtis facility, drawing heavily on design features from the Free Worlds League's Paramour MRV. The vehicle entered production in 3069, coinciding with the opening stages of the Jihad. Johnston's timing proved both fortunate and unfortunate. The desperate need for field repair capability during the widespread fighting ensured immediate demand, but the conflicts raging across the Federated Suns also threatened the factory itself.

The Capellan Confederation's Operation Thunderstrike in 3069 brought fighting to New Syrtis and the surrounding Capellan March worlds. While Johnston Industries' security forces helped the Fourth Donegal Guards defend the factory complex, the broader invasion spread captured Jiftys into Capellan hands. The Taurian Concordat similarly recovered nearly a dozen from Davion forces around the Pleiades Cluster during their 3067 incursion. These captures gave neighboring powers access to a vehicle that had been exclusively Federated Suns equipment.

By 3069, Johnston Industries had begun granting limited manufacturing licenses to smaller companies outside the Capellan March, recognizing that demand far exceeded what a single factory could supply during wartime. This expansion of production ensured the Jifty's wider adoption across the Inner Sphere, though the Federated Suns remained its primary operator. The various field modifications that emerged during the Jihad reflected the creativity of technicians adapting the vehicle to rapidly changing battlefield requirements.

The fighting on New Syrtis during the Jihad devastated the Johnston Industries facility in Cilitren on the continent of Mawreddog. The factory was heavily damaged, and the surrounding city was effectively destroyed. Johnston responded by expanding its facilities on Benet III to recover lost production capacity, though plans to restart at least partial production on New Syrtis continued throughout the rebuilding period. The damage to Johnston's primary facility had ripple effects across the company's entire product line, affecting production of vehicles far beyond the Jifty.

The corporate theater surrounding the Jifty also produced controversy. In the latter half of the 3060s, Blue Bull, Inc. produced a blatant copy of the JI-50 called the "Nifty," an ICE-powered knockoff that undercut the Jifty's market position. Johnston Industries attempted to pursue legal action for patent violations, but the chaos of the Jihad prevented any meaningful progress in the courts. The years since proved Johnston's concerns well-founded. The JI-100, a larger successor to the Jifty introduced in 3074, demonstrated that the original design concept was sound enough to scale upward, and military commands gradually upgraded from the JI-50 to the JI-100 where budgets permitted. The Nifty found no lasting place on Federated Suns equipment rosters.

text.deployment: The JI-50 (MG) field modification replaces the standard light machine guns with heavier-caliber weapons, providing improved defensive capability against infantry and light vehicles at close range. This has been the most common field alteration performed on the Jifty, reflecting the reality that recovery crews frequently encountered hostile forces during Jihad operations.

This radical modification sacrifices the vehicle's primary purpose for meaningful defensive firepower, and is typically only performed when the tactical situation demands armed vehicles more than repair capability.
