text.deployment: The JI-50 (Q-Vehicle) is a custom modification rumored to have been designed for ambush operations. It exchanges all cargo capacity for eight SRM-4 launchers and ammunition, converting the innocuous-looking repair vehicle into a devastating close-range combatant. Rumors persist of a Taurian example on Merope configured as an ambush-buster, though such reports remain unconfirmed.

production.manufacturer: Interstellar Expeditions|Napa Tidal Research - Branson United

text.overview: The Jonah JN-002 is a miniaturized submersible designed for deep-water exploration and research in extreme liquid environments. Its origins trace to Ryan Systemics, an oceanographic research subsidiary of the Ryan Cartel, which had specialized in water-world environmental analysis for decades. When the Cartel's financial troubles triggered a liquidation cascade, the working prototype of a new deep-water submarine was nearly lost. The survival of that design, and its eventual transformation into the production Jonah, represents one of the more unlikely industrial recoveries in the Periphery's civilian technology sector. Introduced in 2714 on the oceanic world of Blue Hole, the Jonah carved out a niche market among deep-sea research organizations and resource extraction operations working in environments hostile to standard marine craft. Though never produced in large numbers, the design proved remarkably well-suited to its intended mission.
text.capabilities:
The Jonah is an ultra-light submersible weighing two thousand kilograms, driven by a fusion drive that delivers moderate underwater speed. A cruise pace of four and a flank pace of six are adequate for navigating deep-ocean environments without excessive energy consumption. The hull is rated to withstand depths exceeding ten kilometers, well beyond the operational envelope of most comparable craft. Armor protection is minimal, using a BAR 3 construction rating that prioritizes pressure resistance over combat survivability. The Jonah carries no weapons of any kind.

Standard equipment includes a forward-mounted searchlight, twin manipulator arms at the bow for sample collection and site work, and a rear-mounted remote sensor dispenser. Crew complement is one operator with two passenger positions, giving the vessel a total capacity of three personnel. Life-support systems are rated for continuous dives exceeding ten days without resupply.

The design's chief weaknesses are its absence of defensive armament and its classification as an obsolete, non-standard design throughout much of its operational life. Sourcing replacement components requires custom fabrication or dedicated supply chains. Cargo capacity is limited to under two hundred kilograms, constraining the volume of samples or equipment the sub can carry on a single mission. These limitations narrow the Jonah's appeal to well-supported organizations with established logistics networks.
text.deployment: The JN-002 is manufactured at the Interstellar Expeditions facility on Blue Hole and distributed exclusively to IE member organizations. Its missions center on deep-ocean scientific investigation, underwater resource surveys, and environmental monitoring in liquid environments beyond the reach of surface or near-surface craft. The Jonah has seen deployment across Periphery water worlds where IE-sponsored expeditions regularly operate under conditions requiring sustained deep-dive capability. Its manipulator arms and remote sensor systems make it particularly suited for sample collection and site documentation. Operators outside IE-affiliated networks face significant logistical challenges in sourcing replacement components, effectively limiting the design to well-supplied organizational fleets with dedicated support infrastructure.
text.battleHistory:
Ryan Systemics began as the environmental science arm of the Ryan Cartel, tasked with studying water-world ecosystems and developing filtration technologies for colonial water supplies. As new filtration methods undercut the Cartel's broader profits, Ryan Cartel began liquidating subsidiaries, and Systemics faced dissolution. A working prototype submarine, informally called the Jarvis, had just completed qualification trials when the liquidation began. Trevor Stefanis, a Systemics employee, managed to remove the prototype before the facilities were foreclosed, preserving the only working example of what would eventually become the Jonah.

Decades later, Trevor's great-grandson Unger Stefanis brought the dormant Jarvis design to Napa Tidal Research on Blue Hole in 2714. Pairing with Branson United to establish a manufacturing line, the venture faced immediate production constraints: a single assembly line required eight months to build each vehicle. Despite this bottleneck, sales outpaced production throughout the partnership's existence. The NTR-BU venture collapsed within a decade, around 2724, and the factory fell silent for more than three centuries. The Jonah acquired its obsolete designation during this long dormancy, and surviving units grew increasingly difficult to maintain as original components aged out of any supply chain.

In 3032, Interstellar Expeditions acquired the derelict factory site on Blue Hole. Restoration took fifteen years and over 1.6 billion Kroner, but by the mid-3040s the plant was again producing Jonahs, this time exclusively for IE member corporations. The revival coincided with renewed interstellar exploration activity across the Periphery, and the Jonah found a second generation of customers among teams investigating deep-ocean worlds and resource-rich aquatic environments. During this same period, Unger Stefanis had leveraged the Cokery Isles chain near Blue Hole as a testing ground for underwater purification infrastructure, establishing Blue Hole Bottling and reshaping the local planetary economy in the process.
text.notes: Armor exceeds point limit for 2.0-ton Submarine support vehicle: 5 points > 4.

text.deployment: The UL-10 mounts a front-mounted backhoe as its primary construction apparatus. It is commonly paired with popular dumper vehicles such as the Brunel and Lesseps at excavation and demolition sites. While both of those vehicles mount integral backhoes, many companies supplement them with UL-10s to double their loading speed. The UL-10 is the most widely produced variant in the series and serves as the baseline model for the family.

The UL-11 mounts rock-cutting equipment and is found at nearly every heavy construction site across the rimward Sphere. It is frequently paired with UL-14 Dual Bulldozers to move broken debris in preparation for processing. The combination of a Rock Cutter breaking material and a Dual Bulldozer clearing it has become a standard two-vehicle team on large-scale demolition and site preparation projects.

The UL-12 mounts a massive chainsaw on the end of a backhoe boom, with braces that clasp tree trunks up to a meter in thickness while the blade cuts through. The boom operator can then pivot and drop the tree for trimming and gathering. Common only on worlds where logging is a serious industry, the UL-12 faces stiff competition from dedicated IndustrialMechs such as the Crosscut LoggerMech, resulting in lackluster sales compared to its siblings.

The UL-14 is a dual-blade bulldozer mounting heavy blades on both the front and rear of the chassis. This configuration allows the vehicle to work in both directions without needing to turn around, increasing operator productivity. Many operators consider this a significant profit-earning feature, and it has endeared the UL-14 to construction company executives. The UL-14 is commonly paired with UL-11 Rock Cutters at demolition and site clearing operations.

text.overview: The Knox Armored Car is among the most common civilian security vehicles in the Inner Sphere, descended from a Terran Hegemony transport design known as the Ranger. Built on a reinforced five-ton truck chassis, the Knox provides modest protection against small arms and light criminal weaponry for high-value cargo movements across dozens of inhabited worlds. Its light armament functions primarily as a deterrent, discouraging opportunistic theft while signaling that a convoy is not entirely undefended. The vehicle's low cost and straightforward maintenance requirements have made it the default security transport for planetary constabularies, banking institutions, and commercial enterprises that cannot justify or afford dedicated military vehicles. Knox-type vehicles appear throughout the Inner Sphere in the service of anyone who must move valuable cargo through contested or unstable environments, forming the unglamorous backbone of civilian security logistics from the Succession Wars era onward.
text.capabilities:
The Knox is built on a wheeled medium truck platform powered by an internal combustion engine, giving it adequate performance on improved roads and paved surfaces. Its cruise and flank speeds are sufficient for convoy escort and urban patrol work, keeping pace with commercial traffic without requiring military-grade power plants or maintenance infrastructure. The vehicle's BAR 10 armor provides fifteen total points of protection distributed across its hull and turret, adequate against small arms and fragmentation but offering little resistance to military weapons. This armor level is deliberately matched to the threat environment the Knox is designed for: criminal elements carrying civilian firearms and light anti-vehicle weapons, not organized military opposition.

The Knox mounts a single turret-mounted machine gun with a hundred rounds of ammunition, its primary purpose being visual deterrence rather than combat effectiveness. A basic fire control system supports the gunner with minimal targeting assistance. The vehicle carries 1.5 tons of standard cargo, enough for small payroll shipments, sensitive equipment, or priority personnel. The wheeled drive system performs well on prepared surfaces but restricts the Knox to urban and developed terrain, limiting its utility outside of cities and established road networks. The Knox is explicitly not a combat vehicle, lacking the firepower or armor to engage military opposition and the cargo capacity to serve effectively as an armored personnel carrier.
text.deployment: Knox Armored Cars operate throughout the Inner Sphere, appearing wherever commercial enterprises, planetary governments, or militia organizations require inexpensive armored transport for high-value cargo. Their most common roles are payroll escort, banking transport, and the movement of sensitive equipment across worlds too poor to afford dedicated military security assets. The Knox's prevalence ensures that replacement parts remain widely available, simplifying logistics for operators across multiple factions. The vehicle performs best when treated as a deterrent platform with infantry escort rather than a standalone combat asset, and operators who attempt to use the Knox as a fighting vehicle against military-grade opposition do so at their considerable peril.
text.battleHistory:
The Knox's predecessor, the Ranger, entered service with the Terran Hegemony as a military utility transport. When the Star League collapsed and the Succession Wars fragmented interstellar industry, the basic design survived by transitioning from military to civilian application. Local manufacturers on dozens of worlds adapted the platform to available industrial components, producing Knox-type vehicles from common truck parts and locally fabricated armor plating. The resulting vehicles varied considerably in quality but retained the fundamental characteristics of the original design: light, cheap, and easy to maintain.

Throughout the Succession Wars, planetary militias occasionally pressed Knox cars into limited security roles, a function the design handled adequately as long as it faced only criminal opposition. The growing availability of military-grade hardware in criminal hands, particularly as black market salvage from the constant warfare of the era found its way into civilian channels, steadily eroded the Knox's effectiveness. By the late thirty-first century, well-organized criminal organizations and rogue military units possessed weapons capable of defeating Knox armor with ease, and the lack of any anti-vehicle capability left Knox crews with few options beyond attempting to flee.

The Briggs Armored Car robbery of late 3059 on Alexandria crystallized the problem. A criminal gang with access to surplus Grey Death Legion Battle Armor overwhelmed a Knox convoy despite a BattleMech escort, exploiting the fundamental mismatch between the Knox's civilian armor rating and the capabilities of modern military hardware. The incident attracted commercial and media attention across the Lyran Alliance, generating industry discussion about the gap between the Knox-class civilian security standard and the threat environment that Inner Sphere operators actually faced. This episode directly motivated Gienah Automotive to begin development of the Bailey Armored Car as a credible alternative.

text.overview:
The Koi Heavy Transport is a large wing-in-ground-effect cargo vehicle designed and manufactured by Wakazashi Enterprises for the Draconis Combine's domestic transport market. Introduced in 3056, the Koi was created to address a recognized gap in planetary logistics on Combine worlds where DropShip transport is economically impractical for routine cargo movement. Wakazashi positioned the design for the civilian sector, emphasizing cargo capacity and long-range overwater transit over military utility.

The Koi's enormous two-hundred-forty-ton frame carries over one hundred twenty tons of reconfigurable cargo, and its fusion powerplant provides operational range limited only by crew endurance. Coordinator Theodore Kurita's economic modernization reforms drove demand for precisely this kind of high-capacity domestic transport, and the Koi quickly became a fixture of commercial logistics across the Draconis Combine and neighboring states.
text.capabilities:
The Koi's most significant asset is its cargo flexibility. The main bay accommodates standard freight containers, infantry formations, wheeled and tracked vehicles, or even a single BattleMech, with quick-release flotation tanks and powerful pumps enabling rapid reconfiguration between load types. This versatility makes the Koi useful for planetary militia and light garrison commands that lack dedicated combat transport assets.

Wing-in-ground-effect movement gives the Koi effectively unlimited overwater range. Its amphibious chassis modification allows bay doors to be opened while the vehicle is afloat without risk of flooding, enabling loading and unloading from open coastlines or shallow anchorages with no port infrastructure required. Cruise speed over water is modest, though flank speed is adequate for emergency maneuver away from a threat.

The Koi's limitations are considerable for any military context. It carries no weapons, relying entirely on escorts for protection. All WiGE vehicles are inherently vulnerable to conventional aircraft and aerospace fighters, and the Koi's enormous radar profile makes evasion impossible. Its large size means combat damage while carrying a full load risks catastrophic loss of both cargo and vehicle. The design is also exposed to ground fire if forced to transit near hostile positions at low altitude.
text.deployment: The Koi Heavy Transport serves primarily as a commercial cargo vehicle throughout the Draconis Combine, operated by trading houses, planetary governments, and militia logistics commands. Export units are found across the Inner Sphere wherever cost-effective long-range overwater cargo movement is needed. The design is unarmed and unsuited for frontline service, but its enormous payload makes it an indispensable asset in rear-area logistics and disaster relief operations. On Tabayama, the Hunters International collective operates a large fleet for hunting and agricultural transport across the world's extensive croplands.
text.battleHistory:
Wakazashi Enterprises developed the Koi against a backdrop of rising commercial demand across the Draconis Combine's interior worlds. Coordinator Theodore Kurita's economic modernization program, begun in the decades before the Clan Invasion, created pressure on domestic logistics networks that existing transport infrastructure struggled to meet. Wakazashi, already an established producer of military WiGE vehicles, recognized an opportunity in the civilian cargo market and committed development resources to a purpose-built design.

The Koi entered production at the Wakazashi facility on Dover in 3056 and found ready buyers among planetary governments, trading houses, and militia commands throughout the Combine. Its combination of payload and aquatic flexibility made it especially attractive on worlds with extensive coastlines or inland waterways. The Hunters International collective on Tabayama adopted the design early, using it to move hunting parties and equipment across the world's vast croplands far faster than ground vehicles could manage.

The commercial success of the Koi attracted unwanted attention. In 3061, a factory fire on Dover halted production for three months. Wakazashi executives publicly accused Pesht Motors, the Combine's primary manufacturer of civilian transports, of deliberate sabotage. An investigation confirmed the fire was arson, but no definitive evidence linking Pesht Motors to the incident was produced. Relations between the two corporations have remained strained since, and the disruption gave Wakazashi internal justification to shift some research and development activity off Dover. That decision would later shape how the Koi's military derivatives were developed.

The Koi has continued as a commercial backbone for planetary logistics in the Draconis Combine, with export units reaching neighboring states. Militia commands short on dedicated transport WiGEs have repeatedly pressed civilian Koi units into emergency service during periods of conflict, a role for which the vehicle was not designed but has proven capable of fulfilling.

text.overview: The Korvin Tank emerged in the early 2300s as the Capellan Confederation's purpose-built response to large laser technology. Constructed under the supervision of engineer Wu Han at New Hessen ArmorWorks on New Hessen, the design exploited reverse-engineered Terran Hegemony weapons to give Confederation forces a decisive edge over contemporary armored vehicles. Named in honor of explorer and philosopher Alana Korvin DeVall, the Korvin became the standard battle tank of the Capellan Confederation for much of the 24th century. A 50-ton tracked medium vehicle powered by a fusion engine, it combined energy firepower and solid speed in a package uncommon among vehicles of the era. The Korvin served Capellan forces for over two centuries across multiple production sites.
text.capabilities:
The Korvin's primary identity is as an energy weapon platform. The Wu Heavy Laser in the turret delivers considerable damage at medium and longer ranges without ammunition dependency, while a Longbow LRM-10 rack provides indirect fire support to engage targets beyond the laser's effective reach. Five Browning Large Caliber machine guns are positioned to cover all arcs of the vehicle, deterring infantry from closing. The Magna 250 fusion powerplant drives the 50-ton hull to a flank speed of 86 km/h, giving the Korvin the mobility to serve as a flanking unit or pursue retreating forces alongside heavier assets.

Eight tons of ProtecTech 4 armor offers reasonable protection for a medium vehicle, though it falls short of the most heavily armored vehicles in its weight class. The fusion engine, while providing a weight advantage over internal combustion rivals, proved demanding to maintain. Environmental controls and other internal systems are persistent reliability concerns, a consequence of the design's rushed development. The tank's unusual silhouette, another artifact of that rapid design process, makes it easily recognizable on the battlefield but offers no benefit in concealment.
text.deployment: The KRV-2 served in the front-line armored regiments of the Capellan Confederation during the 24th century, where its large laser firepower gave it a genuine edge against the vehicles of the era. As BattleMechs came to dominate the battlefield and armor technology advanced, the KRV-2 transitioned to garrison and militia roles, serving roughly another century and a half in secondary assignments. With the introduction of the KRV-3, most surviving KRV-2s were sold to Periphery states rather than scrapped. Spare parts for the fusion reactor are now extremely scarce, and operational examples are exceptionally rare.
text.battleHistory:
The Korvin's origins trace to the Tikonov Grand Union, which spent decades contesting border systems with the Terran Hegemony. Despite numerous defeats, Tikonov engineers salvaged Hegemony technology from the battlefield and eventually replicated the large laser. Engineer Wu Han oversaw the translation of that achievement into a functional combat vehicle, producing the KRV-2 at New Hessen ArmorWorks in 2367. This second-generation design, named for the philosopher Alana Korvin DeVall, featured a lighter and more powerful fusion engine than its Hessen-series predecessor, increasing top speed by roughly thirty percent. Production later expanded to Capricorn III and Sian with the formation of Wu Industries.

The Korvin served as the backbone of Capellan armored forces through much of the 24th century. Assigned to premier regiments, it gave Confederation armor a genuine advantage in an era when few vehicles mounted adequate protection against large laser fire. The design's prominence helped shape early Capellan armored doctrine, and the tank became a symbol of Confederation military capability. As armor technology improved across the Inner Sphere, however, a single heavy laser was no longer sufficient to dominate the battlefield, and the Korvin was progressively shifted to garrison and militia duties.

Wu Industries introduced the KRV-3 in 2430, attempting to revitalize the aging design with improved performance. The new model performed adequately but could not reverse the Korvin's decline in the face of proliferating BattleMechs. Production on Capricorn III and Sian continued until Wu Industries closed its doors in 2612. Most remaining KRV-2s were sold to Periphery states rather than scrapped, while the design's influence reached even further when the Umayyad Caliphate began producing its own version on Granada in the 29th century.
text.notes: Armor exceeds point limit for 50.0-ton Tracked support vehicle: 105 points > 104.

text.overview: The Lama-Deux is a thirty-ton Medium VTOL manufactured by Pion-Laurier on Chenier and one of the established firefighting platforms in Federated Suns civil emergency service. Introduced in 3022, the Lama-Deux predates its companion design by more than four decades and represents the conventional engineering tradition to which Pion-Laurier returned after its PEQRAF experimental program failed in the early 3060s. The aircraft is designed specifically for combating high-rise and skyscraper fires, mounting dual high-speed water nozzles on cantilever arms that can be operated from the pilot's console or directed remotely by a firefighter positioned inside the burning structure. Lighter and more maneuverable than the Cascatelle, the Lama-Deux excels in dense urban airspace where larger aircraft cannot safely operate, and its range of over a thousand kilometers ensures broad planetary coverage.
text.capabilities:
The Lama-Deux carries just over eleven tons of liquid firefighting agent in its primary cargo bay, delivering it through two high-speed nozzles mounted on cantilever arms extending from the fuselage. These nozzles can be joystick-controlled from the operator's station in the cabin or operated remotely by a firefighter inside the target building, allowing precise directional suppression without requiring the aircraft to enter the most dangerous areas near the building face. Two sprayers mounted on the right and left sides supplement the primary nozzles for broader area coverage, while a mounted searchlight provides illumination for night operations and smoke-heavy environments. The aircraft carries six passengers in addition to its two-person crew, supporting rescue extraction or the insertion of firefighting teams.

The Lama-Deux shares the Cascatelle's cruise and flank speeds despite its smaller size, achieving roughly fifty-four and eighty kilometers per hour respectively. Armor protection is modest at BAR 3, consistent with the lighter construction of a platform not expected to operate in contested airspace. The dual VTOL rotor arrangement provides the hovering stability required for extended stationary positioning alongside a burning high-rise, which is the most demanding operational profile the design was built to handle. The absence of weapons reflects the Lama-Deux's purely civilian role, with no provision for self-defense.
text.deployment: The Lama-Deux serves fire departments in urbanized regions throughout the Federated Suns, with the greatest concentration on worlds featuring dense high-rise construction and skyscraper-heavy metropolitan centers where ground ladder equipment cannot reach the required elevation. Its compact footprint and remote-operable nozzle system make it particularly well suited to airspace-congested environments where larger aircraft cannot maneuver safely near a structure. Civil fire services on industrialized worlds frequently operate Lama-Deux units alongside Cascatelles to provide both precision high-rise suppression and broader area coverage within the same squadron. On smaller or less populated worlds the design's range also supports planetary coverage from a single base, with response times acceptable for most emergency scenarios.
text.battleHistory:
The Lama-Deux entered service with Federated Suns planetary fire departments in 3022, establishing itself as a standard high-rise firefighting platform decades before Pion-Laurier developed the larger Cascatelle. The design's age and proven reliability made it a natural anchor for the manufacturer's product line when the PEQRAF experimental program failed in the early 3060s, and the Lama-Deux's continued production alongside the newer design reflects sustained demand for its specialized urban role. Fire services have found that the Cascatelle and Lama-Deux serve complementary functions, with the latter providing precision suppression capability in confined high-rise environments that the larger aircraft cannot safely enter.

The design was developed to address a category of emergency that conventional ground equipment and ladders cannot reach: fires in tall structures where the building's own suppression systems have failed and the blaze is above the operational ceiling of standard firefighting apparatus. This problem has intensified on heavily urbanized Federated Suns worlds as cities expanded vertically throughout the Succession Wars era, creating a steady demand for platforms like the Lama-Deux. The aircraft's remote nozzle capability was recognized early as a significant safety advantage, allowing operators to suppress fires in areas where smoke or structural instability would make direct approach lethal.

The Lama-Deux remains in production at Pion-Laurier's Chenier facility well into the thirty-second century, evidence of the durability of its basic design. Some fire services have updated individual aircraft with improved communications equipment over the years, but the core airframe and suppression system have required few modifications to remain operationally relevant. Its longevity stands as a counterpoint to Pion-Laurier's PEQRAF misadventure, demonstrating the enduring value of straightforward engineering in civil emergency equipment.

text.overview: The Lesseps Dump Truck is a medium wheeled support vehicle produced by Earthwerks Incorporated, introduced in 2523 to serve the construction and mining industries across the Inner Sphere. At fifty tons, the Lesseps occupies a far more accessible market segment than heavier industrial vehicles, offering sufficient cargo capacity and off-road capability for typical construction operations at a price point that keeps it common across industrial sites throughout settled space. Earthwerks distributes the Lesseps through a network of production facilities scattered across the Inner Sphere, and the design has been a staple of planetary construction and mining firms since its introduction, despite a commercial reputation that has not always been kind to its manufacturer.
text.capabilities:
The Lesseps operates on an electric battery power plant, providing a published range of over thirteen hundred kilometers on a single charge and a continuous operational window of approximately twenty-four hours before recharging is required. Its off-road chassis and controls modification, combined with an all-wheel drive system, allows the vehicle to operate effectively on ungraded terrain typical of active construction and mining sites. The rear dump bed carries up to twenty tons of cargo, and a forward-mounted backhoe provides integrated loading capability. These features make the Lesseps a practical and self-sufficient tool for sites that lack dedicated loading infrastructure.

Protection is limited to two and a half tons of commercial armor at a barrier armor rating of five, leaving the vehicle vulnerable to even modest weapons fire. It carries no armament and relies entirely on distance from hostile forces or armed escort for survivability. The vehicle carries the Bad Reputation design quirk as a formal acknowledgment of documented quality failures that became widely known across the Inner Sphere market, a mechanical and commercial liability that buyers factor into procurement decisions.
text.deployment: The Lesseps is deployed across the Inner Sphere at construction sites, open-pit mines, and light industrial facilities wherever a medium-duty dump vehicle is required. Its affordability and widespread availability through Earthwerks' multi-site distribution network make it the default choice for smaller operations that cannot justify heavier equipment. Military forces have occasionally requisitioned available Lesseps vehicles for logistics support in low-intensity operations, particularly for debris clearing and supply movement in rear areas where its limited protection is less of a liability.
text.battleHistory:
Earthwerks Incorporated introduced the Lesseps in 2523, positioning it as a practical medium-duty work vehicle for construction and light mining operations. Over the following centuries it became one of the most commonly encountered support vehicles in settled space, with Earthwerks maintaining production at numerous sites across the Inner Sphere to meet sustained demand from the construction and resource extraction industries.

That established commercial position was severely tested in the late thirtieth century when a series of battery fires damaged the vehicle's reputation across the Inner Sphere. Investigation revealed that a subcontractor based in the Capellan Confederation had supplied faulty battery packs prone to overheating after prolonged use, a defect introduced when cheaper materials were substituted in an effort to reduce production costs. Earthwerks moved quickly to replace all affected units once the source of the failures was identified, but competitors seized on the negative publicity to draw customers away from the Lesseps line. The commercial stigma lingered well beyond the correction of the underlying defect, cementing the Bad Reputation design quirk as a reflection of buyer skepticism that continued to affect sales into the thirty-first century and beyond.

text.overview: The Lewis Skimmer Bus is a large civilian hover transport produced by S. L. Lewis, Incorporated, introduced in 3026 near the close of the Third Succession War. Built as the company's first entry into the civilian passenger market after the success of the Savannah Master hovercraft, the Lewis offers high capacity passenger transport with meaningful cargo flexibility. Its large hover chassis provides terrain adaptability beyond what wheeled or tracked alternatives can offer, and its fuel cell powertrain made it an appealing option for transit operators concerned with air quality and fuel availability. The vehicle's introduction coincided with a modest period of economic recovery in the Lyran Commonwealth, where renewed interest in civilian infrastructure created demand for capable and cost-effective mass transit platforms.
text.capabilities:
The Lewis Skimmer Bus is built on a large hover chassis and weighs 80 tons fully equipped. Its fuel cell electric power plant provides clean, quiet operation well suited to enclosed transit environments and urban areas with air quality restrictions. The plant delivers enough power to push the vehicle to flank speeds exceeding 160 km/h, making it one of the faster large hover transports in civilian service. Cargo is accessed through a rear door, with 18.05 tons of standard cargo capacity available alongside seating for 86 passengers.

The vehicle is crewed by three personnel: a driver and two stewards who manage passengers and cargo. BAR 4 commercial armor covers the exterior, providing protection against minor collisions and road hazards. The Lewis carries no armament. The primary operational constraints are its large footprint, which limits access to narrow urban streets and passages, and its weight class, which requires dedicated maintenance facilities capable of servicing large support vehicles. A small number of plainclothes security personnel can be placed among the passengers when valuable cargo requires discreet protection.
text.deployment: The Lewis Skimmer Bus operates primarily on high-capacity civilian transit routes in urban and metropolitan areas across the Lyran Commonwealth and former Federated Commonwealth territories. Transit authorities deploy it on high-density inter-district routes and as connectors between population centers where large passenger volumes justify the vehicle's size and maintenance requirements. The rear cargo bay makes the Lewis attractive for mixed passenger-and-freight operators on routes where dedicated freight vehicles are impractical. When carrying high-value cargo, operators may deploy plainclothes security personnel among the passengers, allowing protection without any outward military appearance. Deployment is generally limited to regions with maintenance facilities equipped for large support vehicles.
text.battleHistory:
S. L. Lewis, Incorporated was established in or shortly after 3017 by Samuel Laurence Lewis, a former warrant officer who recovered a large cache of Omni 25 fusion engines from an abandoned Star League supply depot found while serving aboard the JumpShip Winnetka. Rather than liquidating the salvage, Lewis used the engines to found a manufacturing company and develop the Savannah Master hovercraft for the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces. The military vehicle proved successful, and the company expanded into engine production and later the civilian market.

The Lewis Skimmer Bus entered production on Carlisle in 3026, representing the company's first civilian product. Shortly after its introduction, commanders on Severn pressed available Lewis buses into service as improvised infantry transports, ferrying troops to and from the front lines as the Third Succession War wound down and dedicated APCs ran short. The episode showed that the large hover platform could serve adequately in auxiliary military roles despite having no such intent in its design.

The vehicle found commercial success in the Lyran Commonwealth and beyond. During the FedCom era, the Carlisle facility operated under Federated Commonwealth ownership and continued production through the Clan Invasion. Following the breakup of the Federated Commonwealth, ownership reverted to the Lyran Alliance, and the Lewis remained in production through the Jihad and into the Republic era. S. L. Lewis, Inc. diversified over time, expanding its manufacturing footprint and developing the Edasich Omni 25 engine in partnership with Edasich Motors to sustain its vehicle lines when the original salvaged engine supply was exhausted.

text.deployment: The Series VI serves the most exclusive segment of the luxury VTOL market, with each aircraft custom-built to the buyer's specifications at the New Earth facility. Its amphibious capability has proven particularly popular among wealthy estate owners on waterworlds and coastal retreats. The fusion engine and generous cargo capacity also make it a favored option for corporate shuttle services, where executives require both comfort and operational flexibility during extended planetary travel.

The Series II remains in production at United Airframe's New Earth facility, serving its original niche among corporate executives and the ultra-rich. Despite centuries of production interruptions, demand for the custom-built personal VTOL has never wavered among those who can afford it. The aircraft's compact size and foldable wings make it a practical transport option for executives who travel between worlds, allowing the VTOL to accompany its owner aboard DropShips and JumpShips.

text.overview:
The Lexan Surveillance Helo is a militarized derivative of the Oceanic Series II personal VTOL, developed by Lockheed/CBM Corporation at their Furillo plant. Originally conceived as a reconnaissance platform for the experimental Cloud Ten airship carrier, the design evolved from a limited-run prototype into a full production surveillance aircraft.

The prototype first flew in 3076 as an experimental refit of the civilian Series II airframe, incorporating military-grade electronics and light weaponry. The production model, redesigned and introduced in 3080, addressed the prototype's shortcomings while retaining the core surveillance mission. Heavier and more capable than its predecessor, the production Lexan found a receptive market among Lyran Commonwealth planetary militias, law enforcement agencies, and paramilitary organizations seeking an affordable reconnaissance platform.
text.capabilities:
The prototype Lexan weighs fifteen tons and retains the Series II's fusion engine, giving it unlimited range at speeds approaching 230 kilometers per hour. An Angel ECM suite provides electronic protection, while a recon camera serves as the primary sensor package. Two small lasers offer minimal self-defense capability, though the aircraft lacks any fire control system to employ them effectively. BAR 10 commercial armor inherited from the civilian airframe provides the only physical protection.

The production model increases mass to seventeen tons and replaces the experimental Angel ECM with a more reliable Guardian ECM suite paired with a Xilex 12 Wireless communications system. Top speed drops to 194 kilometers per hour, but the aircraft gains significant improvements. An Omni Generation Five fusion engine provides power, while Longanecker E-Series armor replaces the commercial plating. Two Defiance B3S small lasers mounted alongside a recon camera in a chin turret provide observation and self-defense capability. The production Lexan uses composite rotor materials and advanced fabrication techniques that reduce audible emissions by fifty percent over the Oceanic series. A Suresight camera system gives the operator four configurable displays capable of detecting targets at eighteen kilometers, with indirect LRM targeting telemetry available through a software bypass that voids the warranty.
text.deployment: The production Lexan Surveillance VTOL has become a fixture of Lyran Commonwealth planetary militias, with notable concentrations in the Timbuktu Theater, Melissia Theater, Coventry Province, and Arc-Royal Province. Law enforcement agencies and paramilitary organizations have also adopted the aircraft in significant numbers. Lockheed/CBM has aggressively marketed the design through multi-unit discounts, reduced-price upgrades, and other incentives to bolster sales. Despite commercial success in non-military markets, the LCAF has declined to adopt the Lexan for frontline service, reportedly due to its lack of a dedicated targeting and tracking system.
text.battleHistory:
The Lexan Surveillance Helo traces its origins to the Cloud Nine airship disaster of 3065, which silenced interest in airship-based fighter carriers for nearly a decade. In 3074, Rebecca Cardinali, engineering director for Lockheed/CBM's personal VTOL division, attended the fifty-seventh annual EECEIECE conference. There she met Joseph Akron, cousin to Count Douglas Fassei of Cal-Boeing. A late-night debate fueled by several bottles of wine produced an unlikely collaboration when the two engineers argued over whether the Cloud Nine could have been a viable carrier platform.

Two months later, in September 3074, Cardinali presented the Lockheed/CBM regional board of directors with plans for a militarized version of the Lexan Oceanic Series II. The board approved the project immediately, granting Cardinali an expanded staff and budget with the caveat that sixteen functional prototypes be delivered by October 3075. The tight timeline forced compromises. Planned stealth armor was sacrificed for a prototype Angel ECM suite, and an ER small laser was replaced with standard small lasers lacking fire control. Meanwhile, Akron convinced his uncle to finance a new airship carrier, the Cloud Ten, as a demonstration platform.

Six prototype Lexans entered field trials with the Cloud Ten in January 3076, touring remote Lyran Alliance worlds to test surveillance and information-gathering capabilities. The prototype's Angel ECM proved expensive and its lack of proper fire control limited operational flexibility, prompting Lockheed/CBM to develop a redesigned production variant. Company executives embraced a cost-reduction philosophy, dropping the Angel ECM for the proven Guardian suite and adding a proper chin turret with integrated weapons and camera. The revamped aircraft entered production in 3080 and quickly attracted orders from law enforcement, paramilitary groups, and planetary militia commands throughout the Lyran Commonwealth.

text.overview: The Limpet is a four-ton infantry half-track produced by Buda Imperial Vehicles for the Draconis Combine. Introduced in 2715, the design is a near-exact copy of the Taurian Concordat's Rock Rover, adapted to meet Combine procurement requirements. Buda Imperial Vehicles, an established military vehicle manufacturer for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery, made minimal modifications to the proven Rock Rover platform. The Limpet fills the same infantry transport and fire support niche as its Taurian predecessor, providing mechanized infantry formations with a small, durable platform for urban and rough terrain operations. The vehicle has seen widespread service across Combine garrison forces, valued for its simplicity and ease of maintenance.
text.capabilities:
The Limpet shares the Rock Rover's basic layout and performance characteristics, including its half-track drivetrain, electric fuel cell engine, and BAR 8 rated armor protection. The vehicle's small size and tracked rear section allow it to traverse difficult terrain while maintaining a low profile suitable for urban operations.

The primary difference between the Limpet and its Taurian counterpart lies in the turret armament. Where the Rock Rover mounts a support laser, the Limpet substitutes a short-range missile launcher. This change reflects Combine infantry doctrine's preference for missile-based fire support at close range, trading sustained laser fire for greater impact per volley. The two pintle-mounted auto-rifles and advanced fire control system are retained from the original design. The Limpet carries the same infantry compartment as the Rock Rover, accommodating a full squad of infantry with their equipment through a rear-mounted door. The fuel cell powerplant provides adequate range for garrison patrol and convoy escort duties without the logistical burden of more complex engine types.
text.deployment: The Limpet serves Draconis Combine mechanized infantry formations as a light transport and fire support platform. Its SRM armament provides close-range punch suited to the urban and garrison operations typical of its deployment profile. The vehicle is most commonly found in planetary militia and second-line units throughout the Combine's interior worlds.
text.battleHistory:
Buda Imperial Vehicles introduced the Limpet in 2715, drawing heavily from Pinard Electric Motors' successful Rock Rover design. The decision to produce what amounted to a near-copy reflected the pragmatic approach common among Combine military manufacturers during the Star League era, when proven designs were often adapted rather than developed from scratch.

Production was centered at Buda Imperial Vehicles' facilities on Luthien, ensuring steady output under direct Combine oversight. The vehicle served DCMS garrison and militia forces through the Star League period and across the Succession Wars, providing a reliable infantry transport for second-line formations. The Limpet's simple construction and use of readily available components helped it weather the technological decline of the Succession Wars better than more sophisticated designs.

Manufacturing continued through the Clan Invasion and Civil War eras before ceasing around the onset of the Jihad. Buda Imperial Vehicles' Luthien facilities suffered damage during the Jihad along with most major defense industries on the planet, though they were eventually restored. The Limpet's long production run and widespread distribution across Combine garrison forces ensured that existing vehicles remained in service well beyond the end of new production.

text.overview: The LRM Carrier is a sixty-ton tracked combat vehicle designed to deliver massed long-range missile fire at minimal cost. Developed by the Quikscell Company as a modernized successor to primitive Age of War designs dating back to the 2440s, the current production model entered service around 2470 and has remained in continuous use ever since. Manufactured by nearly every major military supplier across the Inner Sphere, the LRM Carrier fills the role of cheap, expendable indirect fire support in armies that cannot afford dedicated artillery assets. Its reputation as a disposable weapons platform belies its effectiveness when properly employed in massed formations, where concentrated volleys of missiles can devastate even heavily armored targets.
text.capabilities:
The primitive LRM Carrier represents the original Age of War design developed by Quik Products Inc around 2440. Built as a fifty-five-ton support vehicle using primitive construction methods, it mounts three LRM-20 launchers behind BAR 6 armor rated for battlefield protection but far below modern military standards. The InterComBust 180 engine and basic fire control systems perform adequately but lack the refinements of later production models.

Advanced fire control systems partially compensate for the crude construction, and the design's straightforward maintenance requirements made it accessible to militaries with limited technical infrastructure. These vehicles were rendered obsolete by the modernized carriers that entered production around 2580, though a handful survived in Periphery arsenals for decades afterward.
text.deployment: The primitive LRM Carrier served during the Age of War era, providing massed missile fire for armies still relying on pre-spaceflight military technology. Quik Products Inc manufactured these vehicles primarily on Ares and Pandora. The design was rendered obsolete by modernized carriers around 2580 but established the weapons carrier concept that would endure for centuries.
text.battleHistory:
The origins of the modern missile carrier stretch back to the Age of War, when Quik Products Inc developed the first standardized tracked platforms for massed missile delivery. These early designs, constructed using primitive technology, were crude but effective, establishing the basic formula of maximum firepower on a minimal chassis that would define the weapons carrier concept for centuries. As Quik Products evolved into the Quikscell Company, the original primitive carriers were refined into the modern designs that entered widespread service by the twenty-fifth century.

During the Succession Wars, the desperate need for cheap fire support led dozens of manufacturers across the Inner Sphere to produce their own versions, many of them little more than unauthorized copies of Quikscell designs built to even lower quality standards. Shortly before the Fourth Succession War, Quikscell launched a series of lawsuits against these clone manufacturers, successfully shutting down many smaller competitors and forcing larger firms to cease production of derivative designs. The company further consolidated its market dominance by offering to exchange any non-Quikscell carrier for legitimate replacement vehicles and parts, effectively cornering the missile carrier market. One company not targeted by the legal attacks was Joint Equipment Systems, which had negotiated in good faith with Quik Products Inc centuries before.

LRM Carrier production spread across an extensive network of facilities. Quikscell plants on Ares, Kalidasa, Layover, Oliver, Pandora, and Broken Wheel turned out thousands of units across every era. Joint Equipment Systems on Alshain, Aldis Industries on Terra, Amaris Armored Vehicles on Timbuktu, the King Dumount Defense Facility on Castile, and Maxwell Planetary Defense Consortium on Maxwell all contributed to a production network spanning the entire Inner Sphere.

The first significant modernization came in 3055, when Quikscell introduced an upgraded variant for the Federated Commonwealth. By incorporating ferro-fibrous armor and Artemis IV fire control systems linked to each launcher, engineers dramatically improved missile accuracy while adding a C3 slave unit for networked targeting. The reduced engine size was considered an acceptable trade for the enhanced combat capability. Oliver and Richvale became the primary production sites for this upgrade package.

The Word of Blake produced their own radical revision during the Jihad era, utilizing an extralight fusion engine to boost both speed and armor protection while retaining Artemis IV systems and adding a C3i computer. Aldis Industries on Terra manufactured this variant throughout the Blakist occupation. In the Dark Age, Joint Equipment Systems developed the LRM Carrier C for the Rasalhague Dominion, mounting the launchers in a partial-traverse turret with hardened armor inspired by the success of the Viking IIC. The LRM Carrier's continued evolution across more than six centuries of service stands as sign of the enduring viability of cheap, massed missile platforms in modern warfare.

text.overview: The Luciano White Wolverine is a lightweight arctic crawler designed and manufactured by the Luciano brothers on the frozen Draconis Combine world of Rubigen. First produced in 2554, the vehicle was purpose-built for operation in extreme cold, navigating ice sheets, hard-packed snow, and the treacherous glacier fields that dominate much of Rubigen's surface. What began as a small garage project by two enterprising siblings grew into a regional manufacturing success, with the White Wolverine earning a reputation as the definitive cold-weather utility vehicle. Rugged, affordable, and well suited to frontier conditions, the design found a steady market among colonists and civilian operators on ice-bound worlds across the region.
text.capabilities:
Weighing just eight tons, the White Wolverine is built on a tracked chassis with a snowmobile modification that allows it to traverse deep snow, ice, and uneven frozen terrain with relative ease. A conventional internal combustion engine provides a cruising speed of roughly 43 kilometers per hour and a top speed approaching 65 kilometers per hour, with a petrochemical fuel capacity sufficient for over 1,400 kilometers of range. This gives the vehicle excellent endurance for long-distance travel across Rubigen's vast glacial expanses.

The White Wolverine carries no weapons and relies on commercial-grade armor rated at BAR 6, offering only modest protection against small arms and environmental hazards. A front-mounted searchlight provides visibility during the long periods of darkness common on Rubigen and similar worlds. The vehicle accommodates a crew of two and carries half a ton of cargo, making it suitable for scouting, light transport, and sightseeing operations rather than any combat role. Its lightweight construction is both a strength and a limitation. While it handles well on ice and remains stable in high winds, the minimal armor and complete lack of armament leave it vulnerable in any hostile encounter.
text.deployment: The base White Wolverine is the sole production variant and has remained largely unchanged since its introduction. It is most commonly found on Rubigen itself, where it serves as the primary civilian transport for glacier crossings, supply runs to remote settlements, and recreational tours of the planet's ice fields. Small numbers have been exported to other cold-climate worlds in the former Rasalhague Military District and beyond, though its niche design limits demand to worlds with comparable terrain. The vehicle sees use by civilian operators, local planetary militias for non-combat logistics, and commercial touring companies.
text.battleHistory:
The White Wolverine traces its origins to the Luciano brothers, Giacomo and Romeo, who began tinkering with a derelict Ground Tug they discovered at an abandoned military airfield on Rubigen. Their improvised repair work proved surprisingly effective for the planet's harsh conditions, and the brothers soon opened a small shop servicing and upgrading their neighbors' vehicles. Romeo supplemented their income by offering sightseeing tours through the Bassers Glacier area, while Giacomo remained in the workshop refining his designs.

Giacomo's most significant contribution was the development of a non-intelligent drive assembly. Inspired by a year-long study of insect locomotion, he devised a purely mechanical system that used physical linkages rather than computer processors to coordinate the vehicle's tracks and suspension over rough terrain. The system proved remarkably effective, giving the White Wolverine its signature smooth handling on ice. Giacomo failed to patent the invention, however, and the New Earth Trading Company filed a patent on a nearly identical drive concept only months later, claiming to have solved similar issues with their own vehicle line.

Despite this setback, the Luciano business thrived. Rising demand led to expanded production capabilities, and the brothers broadened their product range to stay competitive. The White Wolverine remained at the core of their catalog, undergoing only minor refinements over the decades. It became the standard arctic crawler on Rubigen and found buyers on other cold-weather worlds throughout the Draconis Combine's Rasalhague Military District.

When Clan Ghost Bear's First Bear Guards conquered Rubigen in April 3052, the Luciano factory continued to operate under new management. The Ghost Bear occupation, and later the formation of the Ghost Bear Dominion, did little to disrupt production of a vehicle that had no military application. The factory transitioned to Rasalhague Dominion oversight in the early thirty-second century, and the White Wolverine remains in production as a workhorse of Rubigen's civilian transport infrastructure.

text.overview: The Magellan Survey Vehicle is the product of Donovan-Miter, a joint venture formed from the partnership between Donovan Limited and Miter Interstellar Research. Conceived as a modern successor to the legacy of the Croyle Systems Cortez, the Magellan reached limited production in the early 3050s and established itself as a commercially accessible planetary survey platform. Donovan-Miter deliberately chose a fuel cell electric engine over fusion power, reducing cost and simplifying maintenance to put capable exploration equipment within reach of smaller organizations. The Series Four is the most commercially successful variant of the Magellan line, featuring an expanded communications suite and optimized cargo configuration that made it the preferred platform for research firms, archaeological expeditions, and planetary survey organizations across the Inner Sphere and beyond.
text.capabilities:
The Magellan Series Four is a 75-ton wheeled support vehicle designed for sustained planetary exploration operations. Its fuel cell electric engine provides a cruising speed of 32 km/h and an operational range of 2,500 kilometers, prioritizing endurance over performance. The vehicle is amphibious, fully environmentally sealed, and carries a rear-mounted lift hoist for cargo handling alongside four searchlights for low-visibility conditions. Twin forward manipulators allow the crew to handle materials without exposing personnel to the environment. Cargo capacity is generous: nearly ten tons of standard cargo through a rear door, plus a side-accessible foot infantry bay for deploying research teams.

Two turret-mounted machine guns provide basic self-defense with a full load of ammunition, managed by basic fire control. The Series Four's expanded communications module includes scanning and recording equipment alongside a small satellite uplink for real-time coordination between multiple field teams, a capability that became the defining advantage of the variant over earlier Magellan models. The Tech D chassis and electric engine reflect the vehicle's commercial origins, though Blackwell Corporation's advances in modular cargo technology partially realized the original SISO vision in later production runs through Slide-In/Slide-Out modular electronics adapted from recovered Star League records.
text.deployment: The Magellan Series Four serves almost exclusively with commercial and scientific organizations. Interstellar Expeditions maintains the largest fleet, deploying Series Fours as primary platforms for archaeological and planetary survey operations throughout known space. Corporate research firms, planetary survey bureaus, and independent exploration outfits rely on the design for its combination of environmental adaptability, long operational range, and affordability. The Republic of the Sphere operates a smaller number in support of Explorer Corps activities. The fuel cell engine makes the Series Four accessible to organizations that cannot sustain fusion-powered vehicles, significantly broadening the market for capable survey equipment.
text.battleHistory:
The Magellan program grew from Donovan Limited's chance discovery of a derelict Cortez on CJW-7228 in the mid-3040s. Recognizing the potential for a modern successor, Donovan Limited's board partnered with Miter Interstellar Research to attempt a reverse-engineering effort. Miter's team found certain elements of the Cortez's design, particularly the SISO cargo architecture, beyond their technical capability to replicate. Rather than abandon the project, Donovan-Miter took a practical route: replacing fusion power with fuel cell electric propulsion made the design affordable for smaller commercial buyers, and the simplified architecture reached limited production in the early 3050s.

The Clan Invasion nearly ended the program before it found its footing. Donovan-Miter's contracts collapsed in the chaos of the invasion, and the project was shelved until Interstellar Expeditions, a major archaeological consortium focused on the mysteries of the legendary Minnesota Tribe, provided fresh capital and board seats that restarted development. With IE's backing, the Magellan iterated through several series, with the Series Four emerging as the commercial peak: its expanded communications module with satellite uplink capability made it the standard platform for large-scale multi-team survey operations.

Blackwell Industries' destruction on Outreach during the Jihad closed the door on a planned OmniVehicle variant. However, Blackwell's earlier research into modular technology bore partial fruit beginning in 3072, when Series Fours began leaving production with Slide-In/Slide-Out modular electronics derived from recovered Star League records. This partial achievement of the SISO concept that Donovan-Miter had never been able to fully replicate gave the design renewed relevance in an era of increasing technological recovery.

text.overview: The Mao-Heng Charioteer is a light wheeled patrol vehicle commissioned in 2797 by Chancellor Sandol Quinn of the Capellan Confederation. Designed exclusively for the Palace Guard on Sian, the Mao-Heng was intended as a law enforcement cruiser capable of navigating urban streets under fossil fuel power. Despite its sleek exterior, the vehicle earned a reputation for sluggish handling and underwhelming performance almost immediately after entering service. Production was extremely limited, with fewer than two thousand units completed before the line was shut down. The design languished in obscurity for over two centuries before academic researchers revived it as a modernized police cruiser in the mid-thirty-first century.
text.capabilities:
The Mao-Heng Charioteer is a ten-ton wheeled support vehicle powered by an internal combustion engine. Its top speed of just sixty kilometers per hour makes it one of the slowest patrol vehicles ever fielded, a shortcoming that proved a constant liability during urban policing operations. The vehicle carries no weapons whatsoever, relying entirely on its crew and any embarked personnel to provide armed response. Eight passenger seats allow it to function as a personnel transport for small security details or prisoner transfers, with an additional four hundred kilograms of rear-mounted cargo space for equipment or evidence storage.

Protective armor is minimal, rated at BAR 4, offering only modest resistance to small arms fire and virtually no protection against military-grade weaponry. The two-person crew consists of enlisted, non-rated personnel, reflecting the vehicle's purely civilian law enforcement role. While the Mao-Heng's low operating costs and simple maintenance requirements offered some practical advantages for cash-strapped planetary constabularies, these benefits could not offset its fundamental shortcomings in speed and survivability.
text.deployment: The (Original) designation refers to the initial Mao-Heng Charioteer as produced from 2797 to 2799 under Chancellor Quinn's patronage. This variant carries the Obsolete design quirk for the period of 2801 through 3043, reflecting the two-century gap between the cancellation of first-run production and the vehicle's revival as a modernized police cruiser. The original production run saw exclusive deployment with the Palace Guard and Capellan Hussars on Sian, where the vehicles served in an urban law enforcement capacity until the last unit was retired in 2834.
text.battleHistory:
In early 2797, Chancellor Sandol Quinn personally established the requirements for a new patrol vehicle to serve the Palace Guard on Sian. The specifications called for a wheeled design powered by fossil fuels with a minimum speed of sixty kilometers per hour. Quinn's procurement process attracted considerable controversy, as rumors persisted that wealthy associates with interests in the fossil fuel mining industry had influenced the contract requirements. Multiple companies submitted entries, and despite several more promising candidates, the sleek but sluggish Mao-Heng was selected.

Initial production lasted fewer than two years, yielding less than two thousand vehicles before political upheaval ended the program. When Dame Ilsa Liao came of age in 2801, Quinn abdicated his stewardship of the throne in favor of the rightful Liao heir. Shortly thereafter, production of the Mao-Heng was suspended and eventually cancelled entirely.

For several years afterward, the remaining Mao-Hengs continued to patrol the streets of Sian under the fanatically loyal Capellan Hussars. The vehicles developed a mixed reputation during this period. The most notorious example was Patrol 13, which gained infamy beginning in July 2809 after its fifth consecutive month of being towed away from armed confrontations with Triad malcontents. Historians on Purvo later claimed the vehicle received numerous commendations, though irregularities in their records suggest the awards reflected the uncommon valor of the Hussars assigned to the unlucky cruiser rather than any merit of the vehicle itself. Patrol 13 was the last Mao-Heng decommissioned, finally retired in 2834 and purchased by Duke Jian Kao of Purvo for his personal collection.

The Mao-Heng remained forgotten for over two centuries until 3042, when a team of student researchers led by Professor George Sheng at the Sian Regional Training Center selected the design as a graduation project. Their internally reworked prototype performed well enough that the Ministry of Transportation took notice. Within six months, a contract was awarded to Professor Sheng to oversee construction of a new production line featuring the modernized Mao-Heng. The vehicle was once again designated as a law enforcement standard issue, and production as a police cruiser resumed with plans for it to replace older patrol vehicles across Capellan worlds.
